sections.name: plannedMonthlySpend
sections.what_it_is_for: The single canonical "planned monthly spend": the itemized buckets OR the stated total, whichever is larger (the stated total can include an uncategorized remainder the buckets don't capture).
sections.formula_in_words: The year's planned expenses ÷ 12: the twelve months spendByMonth gives, added up, divided by 12. A bill with its own months counts once in the year, on top of the single monthly figure the person typed; with no such bill this equals the larger of the categories added up and that typed monthly figure.

sections.name: categoryMonthly
sections.what_it_is_for: Canonical per-category planned $/month — the ONE conversion the buckets AND the Budget screen share, so a category's on-screen line item ALWAYS reconciles with its bucket total (build-34 #3).
sections.formula_in_words: 0 when the amount is zero or less. A dollar category: the amount, per month — a once-a-year (non-monthly) category is the yearly amount ÷ 12. A percent category: that percent of the average monthly take-home (pctBaseMonthly) — for a non-monthly one the same, worked as a yearly amount and ÷ 12.

sections.name: spendBuckets
sections.what_it_is_for: Roll the per-category expenses up into the three monthly-normalized buckets.
sections.formula_in_words: With categories: each category's monthly amount (categoryMonthly) is added into fixed, non-monthly or flexible — any other bucket counts as flexible; rows of zero are skipped. With no categories: the three typed bucket totals. Monthly total = the three added.

sections.name: spendByMonth
sections.what_it_is_for: Expenses placed in the calendar months it's actually due (Jan→Dec) — NOT averaged.
sections.formula_in_words: Twelve calendar months: each month's figure is the three groups spendByMonthByBucket gives that month added up — bills & fixed, once in a while, everyday — so a screen that shows the groups and one that shows the month read the same amount. Each monthly category adds its monthly amount to every month (a percent category = that percent of the average monthly take-home). Each non-monthly category adds its yearly amount spread evenly over the months it names — over all twelve when it names none (a percent one = percent × average monthly take-home × 12). While only non-monthly categories exist, the typed bills & fixed and everyday totals are added to every month. With no categories: the three typed buckets' total, every month. Then, when the single typed monthly figure is larger than what the plan puts in every month (the monthly categories, the typed totals counted, and a non-monthly category that names no month at its twelfth), the difference is added to every month; a non-monthly category that names its months is on top of the typed figure, in those months only.

sections.name: totalGrossAnnual
sections.what_it_is_for: Total annual income across every inflow (salary for months worked + bonus + signing + equity + net rental + self-employment/investment/benefits/support/scholarship/other).
sections.formula_in_words: Salary for the year + tips for the year + bonus + signing bonus + stock vesting + net rent + taxed extra in a month × 12 + untaxed extra in a month × 12 + one-off taxed + one-off untaxed + retirement income in a month × 12.

sections.name: taxableAnnual
sections.what_it_is_for: Taxable annual income (excludes non-taxable benefits/support/scholarships) — the base for tax estimates.
sections.formula_in_words: totalGrossAnnual WITHOUT the untaxed parts: salary + tips + bonus + signing bonus + stock vesting + net rent + taxed extra in a month × 12 + one-off taxed + retirement income in a month × 12. The 401(k) is NOT taken off here.

sections.name: monthlyTaxRates
sections.what_it_is_for: The tax rate for each of the twelve months, as a share: the one rate in force in every month — the person's own where they gave one, otherwise the calculated rate.
sections.formula_in_words: Twelve rates, all the same: the rate in force (rateInForce) — the person's own, or the calculated one. A steady income is taxed the same in every month.

sections.name: taxableByCalendarMonth
sections.what_it_is_for: The calendar-year TAXABLE profile (Jan→Dec) — the same placement rules incomeMonthlyGrid uses, extracted so the rate vector and the grid can never drift apart.
sections.formula_in_words: For each calendar month: gross salary + tips (only in months with salary) + net rent ÷ 12 + that month's stock vesting + taxed extra in a month + retirement income; + the bonus in its month (December when none); + the signing bonus in January; + one-off taxed other income in its month; − the household's 401(k) that month. Never below 0.

sections.name: incomeMonthlyGrid
sections.what_it_is_for: A representative 12-month cash-flow grid (Jan→Dec) that honors lumpiness: salary & net rental are steady every month; the annual bonus lands in December; the signing bonus is one-time (January); equity is the level annual vesting spread across the month-of-year its vest dates fall on (so quarterly vesting shows up as quarterly spikes).
sections.formula_in_words: For each calendar month. Earned before 401(k) = that month's taxed income (taxableByCalendarMonth) + that month's 401(k). Untaxed = support + that month's scholarships + benefits in their months + one-off untaxed income in its month. Gross = earned before 401(k) + untaxed − reinvested interest and dividends. Tax = tax on the wages + tax on the rest. The wages, earner by earner (worked in one place, which the Cash flow months read too): an earner who typed a take-home is taxed at their own share — (their yearly gross − their 401(k) for the year − 12 × the typed take-home) ÷ their yearly gross, held between 0 and 1 — so they land exactly what they typed; any other earner's wage × the rate in force (monthlyTaxRates). The rest (earned before 401(k) − the wages) × the rate in force — except that when the rate is the person's own, the month's rent and interest and dividends are left out, because they are not on a payslip. After-tax = gross − tax. Take-home = gross − tax − 401(k).

sections.name: pctBaseMonthly
sections.what_it_is_for: A-1: the %-of-income base = true take-home (after tax AND 401k) — the SAME base the expenses-plan screen uses (modules.tsx SpendingEditor → takeHomeMonthly).
sections.formula_in_words: The twelve months of take-home (incomeMonthlyGrid, take-home) added ÷ 12.

sections.name: rateInForce
sections.what_it_is_for: THE ONE ANSWER every screen reads.
sections.formula_in_words: In this order. (1) The person chose to type a rate: that percent ÷ 100, held between 0 and 1. (2) Yearly salary is above zero and every earner typed a take-home: rate = (yearly salary − 401(k) for the year − yearly take-home, never below 0) ÷ yearly salary, held between 0 and 1. Both of these count as the person's own. (3) Otherwise calculated: federal income tax plus state tax on the yearly taxed income (taxableAnnual) LESS the household's 401(k) contributions for the year — they come off before tax — ÷ the yearly taxed income, by filing status, with the standard deduction. 0 when there is no taxed income. Its words for what the calculated rate covers: federal income tax only — or, when a state rate was entered, federal income tax plus that state rate, written as a percent to two decimals — assuming the standard deduction.

sections.name: spendByMonthByBucket
sections.what_it_is_for: THE MONTH'S PLANNED EXPENSES, BY THE BUDGET'S OWN THREE GROUPS — each calendar month, January first (2026-10-23).
sections.formula_in_words: The month's planned expenses in the budget's three groups (bills and fixed, once in a while, everyday), for each of the 12 calendar months, January first. With categories, each category with an amount above 0 counts; one entered as a percent counts at amount ÷ 100 × the monthly take-home it is a share of (pctBaseMonthly). A once-in-a-while category's yearly amount (its amount, or for a percent that share × 12) falls in the months it names, split equally among them, or spread equally over all 12 when it names none; any other category counts its monthly amount in every month, under bills and fixed when it is a fixed bill and under everyday otherwise. While no category is a monthly one (only once-in-a-while categories), every month also gets the typed bills and fixed total and the typed everyday total, each in its own group. Without categories, every month gets the budget's three monthly totals (spendBuckets). Then every month's everyday expenses gain whatever the monthly spending entered is above what the plan puts in every month: the monthly categories, the typed totals counted above, and a once-in-a-while category that names no month at its twelfth. A once-in-a-while category that names its months is never counted against the monthly spending entered, so it adds to its own months only.

sections.name: monthKey
sections.what_it_is_for: 'YYYY-MM' for a date, read from the local clock — never toISOString, which is UTC.
sections.formula_in_words: A date written as year-month, for example 2026-08.

sections.name: spendByMonth
sections.what_it_is_for: Expenses placed in the calendar months it's actually due (Jan→Dec) — NOT averaged.
sections.formula_in_words: Twelve calendar months: each month's figure is the three groups spendByMonthByBucket gives that month added up — bills & fixed, once in a while, everyday — so a screen that shows the groups and one that shows the month read the same amount. Each monthly category adds its monthly amount to every month (a percent category = that percent of the average monthly take-home). Each non-monthly category adds its yearly amount spread evenly over the months it names — over all twelve when it names none (a percent one = percent × average monthly take-home × 12). While only non-monthly categories exist, the typed bills & fixed and everyday totals are added to every month. With no categories: the three typed buckets' total, every month. Then, when the single typed monthly figure is larger than what the plan puts in every month (the monthly categories, the typed totals counted, and a non-monthly category that names no month at its twelfth), the difference is added to every month; a non-monthly category that names its months is on top of the typed figure, in those months only.

sections.name: actualSpending
sections.what_it_is_for: What was actually spent in a month, debt payments left out: every expense newest first, the five shown, how many more there are and the totals, for all of them or only those entered by hand or only those imported.
sections.formula_in_words: The month's logged expenses, leaving out the category Debt payment, newest first — all of them, or only those entered by hand, or only those imported. Shown = the first 5. Hidden = how many more. Total = all of them added. Hidden total = total − the 5 shown.

sections.name: plannedMonthFlow
sections.what_it_is_for: THE PLAN for this month: the take-home, less each debt, less planned expenses.
sections.formula_in_words: Rows, in this order. Inflow = the monthly take-home handed in. A debt has a row only in a month a payment on it falls in: from the month of its first payment to the month it is paid off (a date not given sets no bound), and for a debt due in full only the month it is due, while a balance is owed. One row for each instalment debt with such a payment above zero: minus that payment. Expenses = minus this month's planned expenses when a budget is set — set when handed in as set (the plan holds any expenses, even if none falls in this month, which then reads 0), otherwise when this month plans more than zero — marked your budget; when no budget is set, 0, marked not set. Then one row for each radar debt (a card, a line of credit, a debt due in full) with such a payment above zero: minus that payment — for a debt due in full its whole balance, named "<debt> — due in full". A debt whose payment was never entered (paymentNotEntered), in a month a payment on it falls in, keeps its place as a row at 0, marked payment not entered. Inflow total = the inflow row; outflow = minus the other rows, added up; surplus = every row added up. When any debt's payment was never entered, the surplus and the outflow are not given (no number) and the refusal names the debt: "<debt>'s payment is not entered, so there is no planned surplus — we won't guess one."

sections.name: actualMonthFlow
sections.what_it_is_for: WHAT HAS ACTUALLY HAPPENED: what landed, less only the debts confirmed paid, less what was really spent.
sections.formula_in_words: Rows, in this order. Actual inflow = the monthly take-home handed in. One row for each debt with a payment logged against it this month, or with a payment that falls in this month (from the month of its first payment to the month it is paid off; for a debt due in full, its whole balance in the month it is due, named "<debt> — due in full") and is not zero: minus what was logged as paid against it this month (0 when nothing was), marked paid or not. Other debt payments = debt payments logged this month that match no debt on record, when above zero. Expenses entered by hand = minus the month's logged expenses that were not imported, debt payments left out. Expenses imported from your card = minus the imported ones, shown only when there are any. Debts on the big-ticket radar (cards, lines of credit, debts due in full) are moved to the end. Surplus = every row added up. Inflow total = the inflow row. Outflow = monthOutflow of the month's expenses so far (minus the expense rows, added up) and its debt paid so far (minus the debt rows, added up) — their sum — so the surplus is the inflow total less the outflow.

sections.name: pastMonthFlow
sections.what_it_is_for: A PAST MONTH — what came in, what went out and the surplus — as the Cash flow tab shows it (2026-10-23).
sections.formula_in_words: A past month as the Cash flow tab shows it. The income recorded = the amounts of the income records dated in that month, added up (an amount that is not a number counts 0); the expenses logged = the amounts of the expenses logged in that month (inMonth), added up. What came in = the take-home the month's frozen record states, when there is a frozen record and it states one, else the income recorded. What went out = monthOutflow: with a frozen record, its expenses + its debt paid (each 0 when missing), else the expenses logged. Surplus = what came in − what went out.

sections.name: upcomingBills
sections.what_it_is_for: The dated bills coming due over the next year, each with the day the money must be there, what the month table has there by that day and how much short it would be.
sections.formula_in_words: Bills = each non-monthly budget category, once for every month it names (January when it names none): amount = its yearly amount ÷ the number of months named (a percent one = percent × the take-home the month table carries over its twelve months), on its due day (the 1st when none), at its date this year, or next year when its month is past (nextOccurrence) — a date already passed this month is not returned — in the year it names, when it names one. Only bills due from today to the horizon (365 days when none is given) are returned, soonest first. Need-by date = due date − 2 days; ask-by date = need-by − 10 days. Money available by the need-by date = what the month table handed in has there by that day: the End of the month before the day's month (the starting balance — the first month's End − its In + its Out — when the day is in the first month; that starting balance for a day before the table, the last month's End for a day after it) + every item of the day's month dated on or before the day (an income with a day added; a bill that is not regular money taken away, on its day, the 1st when it has none) + the lower of 0 and that month's regular money (its In − its Out − the dated incomes + the dated bills). Regular money = the everyday expenses and the monthly debt payments, and every income with no day. Less every bill listed before this one that is due after its need-by date and on or before its due date. Shortfall = bill − available, never below 0. Who covers it = your family when family support is one of the income sources, otherwise your savings or a backup.

Regular money = the everyday expenses and the monthly debt payments on the bill side, and every income with no day.

sections.name: cashflowYear
sections.what_it_is_for: Build the 12-month cash-flow picture.
sections.formula_in_words: Twelve months starting with the current one. Taxed income each month = that calendar month's gross salary + tips (only in months with salary) + self-employment + net rent ÷ 12 + interest and dividends ÷ 12 + other income when taxable + that month's stock vesting + retirement income; plus the bonus in its month (December when none is set); a signing bonus in the first month; one-off other income in its month. Untaxed = benefits in their months + support + untaxed other income + scholarships (monthly, or in their months, or ÷ 12 when they name none) + loans in their months (the first month when they name none). Inflow = taxed × (1 − the rate in force) + untaxed. Outflow = the planned expenses for that calendar month (spendByMonth). The balance starts at the starting balance and each month adds inflow − outflow. Short months = those ending below zero. Lowest balance = the smallest month-end. Dated items that fall outside the twelve months are counted, not included.

sections.formula_in_words: With no limit, or a limit of zero or less: no share used and no status. Otherwise share used = balance ÷ limit, rounded to three decimals; status good at 30% or under, caution above 30% up to 50%, high above 50%.

sections.name: categoryMonthly
sections.what_it_is_for: Canonical per-category planned $/month — the ONE conversion the buckets AND the Budget screen share, so a category's on-screen line item ALWAYS reconciles with its bucket total (build-34 #3).
sections.formula_in_words: 0 when the amount is zero or less. A dollar category: the amount, per month — a once-a-year (non-monthly) category is the yearly amount ÷ 12. A percent category: that percent of the average monthly take-home (pctBaseMonthly) — for a non-monthly one the same, worked as a yearly amount and ÷ 12.

sections.name: spendBuckets
sections.what_it_is_for: Roll the per-category expenses up into the three monthly-normalized buckets.
sections.formula_in_words: With categories: each category's monthly amount (categoryMonthly) is added into fixed, non-monthly or flexible — any other bucket counts as flexible; rows of zero are skipped. With no categories: the three typed bucket totals. Monthly total = the three added.

sections.name: spendByMonth
sections.what_it_is_for: Expenses placed in the calendar months it's actually due (Jan→Dec) — NOT averaged.
sections.formula_in_words: Twelve calendar months: each month's figure is the three groups spendByMonthByBucket gives that month added up — bills & fixed, once in a while, everyday — so a screen that shows the groups and one that shows the month read the same amount. Each monthly category adds its monthly amount to every month (a percent category = that percent of the average monthly take-home). Each non-monthly category adds its yearly amount spread evenly over the months it names — over all twelve when it names none (a percent one = percent × average monthly take-home × 12). While only non-monthly categories exist, the typed bills & fixed and everyday totals are added to every month. With no categories: the three typed buckets' total, every month. Then, when the single typed monthly figure is larger than what the plan puts in every month (the monthly categories, the typed totals counted, and a non-monthly category that names no month at its twelfth), the difference is added to every month; a non-monthly category that names its months is on top of the typed figure, in those months only.

sections.name: equityRowValue
sections.what_it_is_for: Value of one vesting-schedule row.
sections.formula_in_words: An option: shares × (market price − strike price), never below 0. Any other grant: shares × price.

sections.name: rsuAnnual
sections.what_it_is_for: Annual equity-comp run-rate: total scheduled value spread over the years it vests across (a level annual figure for the income estimate).
sections.formula_in_words: With vesting rows: their total value ÷ the number of different years in which rows with a value vest (at least 1). With none: shares × price, as typed.

sections.name: totalGrossAnnual
sections.what_it_is_for: Total annual income across every inflow (salary for months worked + bonus + signing + equity + net rental + self-employment/investment/benefits/support/scholarship/other).
sections.formula_in_words: Salary for the year + tips for the year + bonus + signing bonus + stock vesting + net rent + taxed extra in a month × 12 + untaxed extra in a month × 12 + one-off taxed + one-off untaxed + retirement income in a month × 12.

sections.name: taxableAnnual
sections.what_it_is_for: Taxable annual income (excludes non-taxable benefits/support/scholarships) — the base for tax estimates.
sections.formula_in_words: totalGrossAnnual WITHOUT the untaxed parts: salary + tips + bonus + signing bonus + stock vesting + net rent + taxed extra in a month × 12 + one-off taxed + retirement income in a month × 12. The 401(k) is NOT taken off here.

sections.name: monthlyTaxRates
sections.what_it_is_for: The tax rate for each of the twelve months, as a share: the one rate in force in every month — the person's own where they gave one, otherwise the calculated rate.
sections.formula_in_words: Twelve rates, all the same: the rate in force (rateInForce) — the person's own, or the calculated one. A steady income is taxed the same in every month.

sections.name: taxableByCalendarMonth
sections.what_it_is_for: The calendar-year TAXABLE profile (Jan→Dec) — the same placement rules incomeMonthlyGrid uses, extracted so the rate vector and the grid can never drift apart.
sections.formula_in_words: For each calendar month: gross salary + tips (only in months with salary) + net rent ÷ 12 + that month's stock vesting + taxed extra in a month + retirement income; + the bonus in its month (December when none); + the signing bonus in January; + one-off taxed other income in its month; − the household's 401(k) that month. Never below 0.

sections.name: incomeMonthlyGrid
sections.what_it_is_for: A representative 12-month cash-flow grid (Jan→Dec) that honors lumpiness: salary & net rental are steady every month; the annual bonus lands in December; the signing bonus is one-time (January); equity is the level annual vesting spread across the month-of-year its vest dates fall on (so quarterly vesting shows up as quarterly spikes).
sections.formula_in_words: For each calendar month. Earned before 401(k) = that month's taxed income (taxableByCalendarMonth) + that month's 401(k). Untaxed = support + that month's scholarships + benefits in their months + one-off untaxed income in its month. Gross = earned before 401(k) + untaxed − reinvested interest and dividends. Tax = tax on the wages + tax on the rest. The wages, earner by earner (worked in one place, which the Cash flow months read too): an earner who typed a take-home is taxed at their own share — (their yearly gross − their 401(k) for the year − 12 × the typed take-home) ÷ their yearly gross, held between 0 and 1 — so they land exactly what they typed; any other earner's wage × the rate in force (monthlyTaxRates). The rest (earned before 401(k) − the wages) × the rate in force — except that when the rate is the person's own, the month's rent and interest and dividends are left out, because they are not on a payslip. After-tax = gross − tax. Take-home = gross − tax − 401(k).

sections.name: pctBaseMonthly
sections.what_it_is_for: A-1: the %-of-income base = true take-home (after tax AND 401k) — the SAME base the expenses-plan screen uses (modules.tsx SpendingEditor → takeHomeMonthly).
sections.formula_in_words: The twelve months of take-home (incomeMonthlyGrid, take-home) added ÷ 12.

sections.name: rateInForce
sections.what_it_is_for: THE ONE ANSWER every screen reads.
sections.formula_in_words: In this order. (1) The person chose to type a rate: that percent ÷ 100, held between 0 and 1. (2) Yearly salary is above zero and every earner typed a take-home: rate = (yearly salary − 401(k) for the year − yearly take-home, never below 0) ÷ yearly salary, held between 0 and 1. Both of these count as the person's own. (3) Otherwise calculated: federal income tax plus state tax on the yearly taxed income (taxableAnnual) LESS the household's 401(k) contributions for the year — they come off before tax — ÷ the yearly taxed income, by filing status, with the standard deduction. 0 when there is no taxed income. Its words for what the calculated rate covers: federal income tax only — or, when a state rate was entered, federal income tax plus that state rate, written as a percent to two decimals — assuming the standard deduction.

sections.name: spendByMonthByBucket
sections.what_it_is_for: THE MONTH'S PLANNED EXPENSES, BY THE BUDGET'S OWN THREE GROUPS — each calendar month, January first (2026-10-23).
sections.formula_in_words: The month's planned expenses in the budget's three groups (bills and fixed, once in a while, everyday), for each of the 12 calendar months, January first. With categories, each category with an amount above 0 counts; one entered as a percent counts at amount ÷ 100 × the monthly take-home it is a share of (pctBaseMonthly). A once-in-a-while category's yearly amount (its amount, or for a percent that share × 12) falls in the months it names, split equally among them, or spread equally over all 12 when it names none; any other category counts its monthly amount in every month, under bills and fixed when it is a fixed bill and under everyday otherwise. While no category is a monthly one (only once-in-a-while categories), every month also gets the typed bills and fixed total and the typed everyday total, each in its own group. Without categories, every month gets the budget's three monthly totals (spendBuckets). Then every month's everyday expenses gain whatever the monthly spending entered is above what the plan puts in every month: the monthly categories, the typed totals counted above, and a once-in-a-while category that names no month at its twelfth. A once-in-a-while category that names its months is never counted against the monthly spending entered, so it adds to its own months only.

sections.formula_in_words: The gap between two dates in days, never negative.

sections.name: theDebts
sections.what_it_is_for: What do I owe, what does it ask of me each month, when would I be clear of it, and how much have I paid down this year?
sections.formula_in_words: Counts only debts with a balance above zero. Total = their balances added. Minimum in a month = each debt's minimum payment added, a debt due in full counting 0. Payments in a month = each debt's required payment added (requiredPayment). Interest in a month = balance × yearly rate ÷ 12, added over the debts. Plan in a month = the minimums + the extra. Progress: paid down = the debt at the start of the year − the total now; share = paid down ÷ the start-of-year debt; given only when the start-of-year debt and the paid-down amount are both above zero. The payoff plan is payoffPlan, with the extra and the method chosen (highest rate first when none is).

sections.name: payoffPlan
sections.what_it_is_for: Simulate paying off debts with a constant monthly budget (sum of minimums + extra), rolling each cleared debt's freed-up payment into the next per the chosen method.
sections.formula_in_words: Only debts with a balance above zero. A debt due in full is paid in its due month (never earlier than month 1; month 1 when it has no date), with interest = balance × ((1 + yearly rate ÷ 12) to the power of the months until then − 1). The others are walked month by month, for at most 600 months. Each month: every balance grows by balance × yearly rate ÷ 12; the money to pay = the minimums of every debt whose payments have started — including debts already cleared, whose minimums roll on — plus the extra; each debt first gets its minimum (never more than it owes); what is left goes to one debt at a time, highest rate first (avalanche) or smallest balance first (snowball). A debt is cleared when it owes a cent or less. A debt whose first payment date is in the future is not paid until that month, and grows meanwhile. Months = the month the last debt is cleared (or the last lump-sum month, when later); total interest = all the interest charged; it never pays off when anything is still owed at month 600. Order = each debt with the month it is cleared and the interest it cost, earliest first.

sections.name: compareMortgageToTreasury
sections.what_it_is_for: Compare paying `extraMonthly` into the mortgage against putting the same money into Treasuries.
sections.formula_in_words: Nothing unless the balance, the rate and the payment are all above zero. Gap = (mortgage rate − Treasury yield) in percentage points, to two decimals. Too close to call when the gap is under 0.25 points either way; otherwise paying down wins when the gap is positive and Treasuries win when it is negative. Yearly difference = (mortgage rate − Treasury yield) × balance. Lifetime difference — only with an extra above zero and a mortgage that clears both ways — = what (payment + extra) a month grows to at the Treasury yield over the months freed by clearing early, minus what the extra a month grows to at the Treasury yield over all the months the mortgage would otherwise run (futureValue, amortise).

sections.name: monthsToClear
sections.what_it_is_for: How many months it takes to clear a balance at a given yearly rate and monthly payment, or never when the payment does not cover the interest.
sections.formula_in_words: 0 when nothing is owed. No answer when the payment is zero or less, or when it does not exceed the first month's interest (balance × yearly rate ÷ 12) — the debt would never clear. With no interest: balance ÷ payment, rounded up. Otherwise log(payment ÷ (payment − balance × monthly rate)) ÷ log(1 + monthly rate), rounded up to a whole month.

sections.name: loanPayment
sections.what_it_is_for: UNIT LANDMINE (P0): `aprPct` is a PERCENT (7 = 7%), unlike Debt.interest_rate_apr which is a DECIMAL (0.07).
sections.formula_in_words: Months = years × 12, rounded to a whole number; monthly rate = the yearly percent ÷ 100 ÷ 12. All zero when the amount borrowed or the months are zero or less. Payment = amount × monthly rate ÷ (1 − (1 + monthly rate) to the power −months); with no interest, amount ÷ months. Total paid = payment × months. Total interest = total paid − amount.

sections.name: monthsToClear
sections.what_it_is_for: How many months it takes to clear a balance at a given yearly rate and monthly payment, or never when the payment does not cover the interest.
sections.formula_in_words: 0 when nothing is owed. No answer when the payment is zero or less, or when it does not exceed the first month's interest (balance × yearly rate ÷ 12) — the debt would never clear. With no interest: balance ÷ payment, rounded up. Otherwise log(payment ÷ (payment − balance × monthly rate)) ÷ log(1 + monthly rate), rounded up to a whole month.

sections.name: paymentToClearBy
sections.what_it_is_for: Monthly payment that clears `principal` in `months` at decimal APR (amortization).
sections.formula_in_words: 0 when nothing is owed or the months are zero or less. Payment = balance × monthly rate ÷ (1 − (1 + monthly rate) to the power −months), monthly rate = yearly rate ÷ 12; with no interest, balance ÷ months. Rounded UP to the cent.

sections.name: payoffPlan
sections.what_it_is_for: Simulate paying off debts with a constant monthly budget (sum of minimums + extra), rolling each cleared debt's freed-up payment into the next per the chosen method.
sections.formula_in_words: Only debts with a balance above zero. A debt due in full is paid in its due month (never earlier than month 1; month 1 when it has no date), with interest = balance × ((1 + yearly rate ÷ 12) to the power of the months until then − 1). The others are walked month by month, for at most 600 months. Each month: every balance grows by balance × yearly rate ÷ 12; the money to pay = the minimums of every debt whose payments have started — including debts already cleared, whose minimums roll on — plus the extra; each debt first gets its minimum (never more than it owes); what is left goes to one debt at a time, highest rate first (avalanche) or smallest balance first (snowball). A debt is cleared when it owes a cent or less. A debt whose first payment date is in the future is not paid until that month, and grows meanwhile. Months = the month the last debt is cleared (or the last lump-sum month, when later); total interest = all the interest charged; it never pays off when anything is still owed at month 600. Order = each debt with the month it is cleared and the interest it cost, earliest first.

sections.name: applyTransaction
sections.what_it_is_for: Apply one transaction to the accounts (pure).
sections.formula_in_words: What one record does to the accounts. Adjustment: nothing. Opening position: adds the shares at their price as a purchase. Opening cash: sets the account's cash to the amount. Deposit, withdrawal or fee: the cash changes by the money the record moved into the account — up by the amount for a deposit, down by the amount for a withdrawal or a fee; when the record says which way the money went, its size counts that way (a fee refund raises the cash, a deposit reversal lowers it), otherwise the amount counts with the sign it was stored with; a record whose amount is not on record changes nothing. Buy: the shares added as a purchase at their price, and the money moved inside the account (2026-10-23): what the shares cost, shares × price × the shares in one contract the record carries (an option's 100 unless its holding states otherwise, 2026-10-23; 1 for anything else), and the fee the price does not carry (feeNotInPrice) — for an account that keeps its own cash (usesSleeve) the cash goes down by the cost and the fee; a total the person typed goes down by the fee alone (the cost moved inside it); the total of an account built from its holdings is rebuilt from them, and a linked account's total is the broker's and is left as it is; an account whose cash was never entered keeps it not entered. Sale with shares: sells at most the shares held (when a purchase has no share count, so the shares held are unknown, the sale stands as recorded), earliest purchases reduced first; the money moved the same way: what the shares sold brought in, shares sold × price × the shares in one contract the record carries, less the fee the price does not carry — the cash up by that for an account that keeps its own cash, a typed total down by the fee alone, a derived or linked total as above; a sale with no shares but an amount lowers the balance by the amount, never below 0. Transfer: the account it is written on changes by the money the record moved into it — down by the amount, or up when the record says the money came in — and the receiving account, when there is one, by the same amount the other way; nothing when the amount is not on record. Transfer of a holding: the whole holding moves to the other account. Dividend, interest or coupon: when reinvested with shares and a price, a purchase is added to a holding already there; otherwise the cash changes by the money the record moved into the account — up by the amount, down when the record says the money left (a reversal) or the amount was stored below zero; nothing when the amount is not on record.

sections.name: maturityParts
sections.what_it_is_for: A maturity date read as a real calendar day (year, month, day), or nothing when it is missing, written another way, or impossible.
sections.formula_in_words: A maturity date read as a real calendar day: its year, month and day. This is the one reading of a maturity date (MK-NW-F-124 maturityParts): spaces round the text are ignored; then it must be a year, a two-digit month and a two-digit day joined by dashes, or a year and two-digit month alone, read as that month's first day; the month must be 1 to 12 and the day must exist in that month. Anything else — a one-digit month or day, words such as 'tomorrow', a time or other text after the day, a day that does not exist such as February 30 — is no date, and the answer is nothing. Every function that reads a maturity date asks this one (outside review OpenAI re-run part 4, 2026-10-13), so a text is a date to all of them or to none.

sections.name: contractMultiplier
sections.what_it_is_for: How many units one contract stands for: 100 for an option unless the holding states its own figure, and 1 for everything else.
sections.formula_in_words: For an option, its own shares per contract when it states a real number above zero (a stated figure counts for an option only, and one that is not finite counts as none — 2026-10-21); otherwise one hundredth for a bond the broker quotes per $100 of face value (its quantity is the face amount and its price is per $100 of it — the same reading the daily record uses); otherwise 100 for an option and 1 for everything else.

sections.name: purchaseDateOnRecord
sections.what_it_is_for: A PURCHASE DATE ON RECORD: a real calendar day written year-month-day, or nothing (2026-10-21; tenet 3, DEC-3523 — unknown is not zero).
sections.formula_in_words: A purchase date on record: what is stored, read with spaces at the ends ignored, when it begins with a date written year-month-day and that date is a day the calendar has (MK-NW-F-124 maturityParts, the app's one reader of a written day) — the answer is that date; otherwise nothing: no date stored, a date written another way, or a day that does not exist, such as 31 February. Unknown is not a date: a missing date is never read as 1 January 1970 or as today.

sections.name: feeNotInPrice
sections.what_it_is_for: THE FEE ON A BUY OR A SALE THAT ITS PRICE DOES NOT ALREADY CARRY, in dollars (2026-10-21).
sections.formula_in_words: The fee on a buy or a sale that its price does not already carry, in dollars (2026-10-21): the record's fee when it is a number above zero and the record does not say the fee is inside its price; otherwise 0 — no fee on record, a fee that is not a number or not above zero, or a fee the record says is inside its price.

sections.name: cashEffect
sections.what_it_is_for: Signed cash effect on the primary account (for display).
sections.formula_in_words: The change in cash from one record, its amount read by the one rule for a stored amount (2026-10-21): the way the record says the money went, else its kind's own way with the sign it was stored with. Deposit: + amount; a deposit the broker sent with a minus (a reversal, stored as gone out): − amount. Sale: + shares × price × the shares in one contract the record carries (1 when it carries none; 1 contract of an option at $3.00 = $300) less the fee the price does not carry (feeNotInPrice, 2026-10-23) — the amount, when that product is zero, with no fee taken off it. Dividend, interest, coupon: + amount; 0 when reinvested. Withdrawal or fee: − amount; + amount when the record says it came in. Buy: − (shares × price × the shares in one contract the record carries + the fee the price does not carry) — 1 contract at $2.50 = −$250. Transfer: − amount; a transfer that names only one account and says it came in (a broker's journal): + amount. A deposit, withdrawal, fee, transfer, dividend, interest or coupon with no amount on record: 0. Anything else: 0.

sections.formula_in_words: The record that undoes one: a new record noting it is the reversal of the first. When the record states which way its money went (in or out), the undo states the other way — except a transfer between two accounts, which is undone by swapping its two accounts and keeps its own direction (flipping it as well would move the money a second time). A deposit → a withdrawal; a withdrawal or a fee → a deposit; a transfer between two accounts → the same transfer the other way, its two accounts swapped; a transfer out with no receiving account → a deposit; a dividend, interest or coupon paid in cash → a withdrawal; an adjustment → itself. Nothing for a buy, a sale, an opening record, a transfer of a holding or a reinvested payment.

sections.name: reviewTransactions
sections.what_it_is_for: Review new transactions against an account's history.
sections.formula_in_words: Flags, in this order; a record is flagged once. (1) Possible duplicate — any new money-out above zero that has an earlier one on the same account with the same amount (within half a cent) and the same payee, 2 days apart or less. (2) For money-out from a LINKED account only — unusually large: with 5 or more money-outs on that account within 90 days of it, at least 3 × their middle value AND at least $500; with fewer than 5, at least $1,000. (3) Otherwise first-time payee — a payee not seen on that account in those 90 days and not on the known list, for $250 or more. (4) Odd pattern — 3 or more money-outs from one account on one day (the new unflagged ones plus earlier ones that day) adding to $1,000 or more.

sections.what_it_is_for: One line per account that pays something, and the total.
sections.formula_in_words: For each account, the first that applies. (2) A bond or CD, by the one rule for its year of interest (yearlyInterestNow): no rate entered → $0, said so (owner A46), marked as assumed; a rate but no year's interest — a bond with a maturity date and no face value — → $0, said to be the face value not entered, marked as assumed; past its maturity date → $0, said to be matured on that date; a face value entered → the rate × the face value; otherwise (a CD bought from the bank typed by its balance, or a bond fund) → the rate × the balance. (3) Cash with a rate above zero: rate × balance. (4) Any other account with a balance above zero is named as not counted; foreign currency is skipped. Yearly income = the rows added.

sections.name: theContributionRoom
sections.what_it_is_for: How much room is left in my 401(k), IRA and HSA this year, and what would fill it?
sections.formula_in_words: Age = this calendar year − birth year; nothing with no birth year. 401(k): limit by age (annual401kLimit); used = monthly 401(k) × 12, never more than the limit; room = limit − used, never below 0. IRA: limit by age (annualIraLimit); used = monthly Roth IRA × 12, never more than the limit; room = limit − used. HSA: the self-only limit by age (annualHsaLimit), 0 when enrolled in Medicare; used = monthly HSA × 12, never more than the limit; room = limit − used. Catch-up flags: 401(k) and IRA at 50 or over; HSA at 55 or over. Months left = 12 − the months already finished this year (January 12, December 1). Per month to fill the 401(k) = room ÷ months left, to the nearest $100.

Safe draw = solveSafeDraw, with average guaranteed income in a month = the rows' total ÷ 12. Draw flag: high when safe draw × 12 ÷ savings is above 4.5%; ok otherwise; none with no savings or no draw. For each of twelve months from the current one: guaranteed total = that month's rows; bills = that month's big bills, everyday expenses left out; safe to spend = guaranteed total + safe draw − bills. This year = the twelve added.

sections.name: propertyUseMap
sections.what_it_is_for: What each property is for — the home lived in, a rental, or a second home — by his rule DEC-1926: a rental only when a rent entry on the Income screen names it; the one marked as the home is the home; with none marked and no use stated on any, the one entered first; every other property is a second home.
sections.formula_in_words: For each real-estate account: rental when a live rent entry names it, or — only when no rent entries were handed in at all (unknown, not none) — when it is stored as a rental. Of the rest: the one marked as the home lived in is home. With none of the rest marked, the one entered first (last in the list) that is not stored as a rental is home — but ONLY when no property at all carries a stated use other than rental (owner, 2026-10-13: a 'primary' mark on a property a rent entry made a rental still counts as a stated use, so it stops this; a stored 'rental' word does not). A property stored as a rental is never made the home this way. Every other property is a second home. A rent entry that names no property makes no property a rental (owner rule DEC-4059d, 2026-10-10 — it used to make the one other property a rental when exactly one remained).

Are the month bars cash flows -- inflow / outflow?
A month is a real calendar month, never a twelfth of a year (founder, 2026-08-28).
A debt payment is counted as an outflow, not as saving (founder, 2026-06-21).
A bill that falls once a year is shown in its own month, never spread.
A debt counts in a month only if a payment falls in that month — the rule This month’s planned surplus (MK-CF-M-002) reads too (2026-10-24).

THE APPROVED DRAWING WINS (2026-10-23, under his rules DEC-3523 tenet 6 and "the newest approval wins", 2026-09-27): cash-flow_v01, approved 2026-09-28 (DEC-0440), draws the month’s take-home as Actual inflow with nothing recorded. The words this row carried — "nothing is assumed to have arrived; a source counts only once it is recorded" (2026-08-28) — are older and stand down. sections.what_it_is_for: This month's inputs, assembled once, for the month's orchestrator: the take-home and its sources, the debts, the planned bills, the budget by group, the expenses logged and what the Plan promises to goals.
sections.formula_in_words: This month's inputs, assembled once for the month's orchestrator (theMonth). The month = the one handed in, else today's on the person's own calendar. Take-home = the dated grid's first cell's money in (0 when missing), with the sources inside it; every debt; planned expenses = that cell's bill items that are bills, added up (each 0 when missing); whether a budget is set = the plan holds any expenses (plannedMonthlySpend above 0), said only when the person's answers are handed in; the planned expenses by group for that month (spendByMonthByBucket), each group in its words (Bills & fixed, Once in a while, Everyday expenses), a group of 0 left out; every expense logged; and what the Plan promises to goals.

sections.what_it_is_for: The Cash flow model every paycheck surface reads — the paycheck year and the dated grid, from the store as it stands, with the same simulation convention as the Retirement cockpit.
sections.formula_in_words: The Cash flow model, from the store as it stands. The budget is the budget as counted (theBudgetCounted: a mortgage in Debts stands the budget's rent or mortgage line down), when the person's answers are entered; the lens, working or retired, is read from it and from the one the person picked. The paycheck year (buildPaycheckYear) is built from that budget, the accounts and the debts, with the Retirement cockpit's simulation: the person's age (68 when not known), to the age the plan runs to (else the age + 5, and at least 92); a mean return of the return assumed (0.055 when not set); a spread of 1.7 × that mean, kept between 0.05 and 0.2; inflation as set (0.025 when not set); a fixed seed of 42 and 1000 paths. The dated grid is datedGridOf for the same budget, the debts and an adopted Roth conversion's tax.

sections.name: plannedMonthFlow
sections.what_it_is_for: THE PLAN for this month: the take-home, less each debt, less planned expenses.
sections.formula_in_words: Rows, in this order. Inflow = the monthly take-home handed in. A debt has a row only in a month a payment on it falls in: from the month of its first payment to the month it is paid off (a date not given sets no bound), and for a debt due in full only the month it is due, while a balance is owed. One row for each instalment debt with such a payment above zero: minus that payment. Expenses = minus this month's planned expenses when a budget is set — set when handed in as set (the plan holds any expenses, even if none falls in this month, which then reads 0), otherwise when this month plans more than zero — marked your budget; when no budget is set, 0, marked not set. Then one row for each radar debt (a card, a line of credit, a debt due in full) with such a payment above zero: minus that payment — for a debt due in full its whole balance, named "<debt> — due in full". A debt whose payment was never entered (paymentNotEntered), in a month a payment on it falls in, keeps its place as a row at 0, marked payment not entered. Inflow total = the inflow row; outflow = minus the other rows, added up; surplus = every row added up. When any debt's payment was never entered, the surplus and the outflow are not given (no number) and the refusal names the debt: "<debt>'s payment is not entered, so there is no planned surplus — we won't guess one."

sections.name: actualMonthFlow
sections.what_it_is_for: WHAT HAS ACTUALLY HAPPENED: what landed, less only the debts confirmed paid, less what was really spent.
sections.formula_in_words: Rows, in this order. Actual inflow = the monthly take-home handed in. One row for each debt with a payment logged against it this month, or with a payment that falls in this month (from the month of its first payment to the month it is paid off; for a debt due in full, its whole balance in the month it is due, named "<debt> — due in full") and is not zero: minus what was logged as paid against it this month (0 when nothing was), marked paid or not. Other debt payments = debt payments logged this month that match no debt on record, when above zero. Expenses entered by hand = minus the month's logged expenses that were not imported, debt payments left out. Expenses imported from your card = minus the imported ones, shown only when there are any. Debts on the big-ticket radar (cards, lines of credit, debts due in full) are moved to the end. Surplus = every row added up. Inflow total = the inflow row. Outflow = monthOutflow of the month's expenses so far (minus the expense rows, added up) and its debt paid so far (minus the debt rows, added up) — their sum — so the surplus is the inflow total less the outflow.

sections.name: pastMonthFlow
sections.what_it_is_for: A PAST MONTH — what came in, what went out and the surplus — as the Cash flow tab shows it (2026-10-23).
sections.formula_in_words: A past month as the Cash flow tab shows it. The income recorded = the amounts of the income records dated in that month, added up (an amount that is not a number counts 0); the expenses logged = the amounts of the expenses logged in that month (inMonth), added up. What came in = the take-home the month's frozen record states, when there is a frozen record and it states one, else the income recorded. What went out = monthOutflow: with a frozen record, its expenses + its debt paid (each 0 when missing), else the expenses logged. Surplus = what came in − what went out.
