sections.name: plannedMonthlySpend
sections.what_it_is_for: The single canonical "planned monthly spend": the itemized buckets OR the stated total, whichever is larger (the stated total can include an uncategorized remainder the buckets don't capture).
sections.formula_in_words: The year's planned expenses ÷ 12: the twelve months spendByMonth gives, added up, divided by 12. A bill with its own months counts once in the year, on top of the single monthly figure the person typed; with no such bill this equals the larger of the categories added up and that typed monthly figure.

sections.name: categoryMonthly
sections.what_it_is_for: Canonical per-category planned $/month — the ONE conversion the buckets AND the Budget screen share, so a category's on-screen line item ALWAYS reconciles with its bucket total (build-34 #3).
sections.formula_in_words: 0 when the amount is zero or less. A dollar category: the amount, per month — a once-a-year (non-monthly) category is the yearly amount ÷ 12. A percent category: that percent of the average monthly take-home (pctBaseMonthly) — for a non-monthly one the same, worked as a yearly amount and ÷ 12.

sections.name: spendBuckets
sections.what_it_is_for: Roll the per-category expenses up into the three monthly-normalized buckets.
sections.formula_in_words: With categories: each category's monthly amount (categoryMonthly) is added into fixed, non-monthly or flexible — any other bucket counts as flexible; rows of zero are skipped. With no categories: the three typed bucket totals. Monthly total = the three added.

sections.name: spendByMonth
sections.what_it_is_for: Expenses placed in the calendar months it's actually due (Jan→Dec) — NOT averaged.
sections.formula_in_words: Twelve calendar months: each month's figure is the three groups spendByMonthByBucket gives that month added up — bills & fixed, once in a while, everyday — so a screen that shows the groups and one that shows the month read the same amount. Each monthly category adds its monthly amount to every month (a percent category = that percent of the average monthly take-home). Each non-monthly category adds its yearly amount spread evenly over the months it names — over all twelve when it names none (a percent one = percent × average monthly take-home × 12). While only non-monthly categories exist, the typed bills & fixed and everyday totals are added to every month. With no categories: the three typed buckets' total, every month. Then, when the single typed monthly figure is larger than what the plan puts in every month (the monthly categories, the typed totals counted, and a non-monthly category that names no month at its twelfth), the difference is added to every month; a non-monthly category that names its months is on top of the typed figure, in those months only.

sections.name: totalGrossAnnual
sections.what_it_is_for: Total annual income across every inflow (salary for months worked + bonus + signing + equity + net rental + self-employment/investment/benefits/support/scholarship/other).
sections.formula_in_words: Salary for the year + tips for the year + bonus + signing bonus + stock vesting + net rent + taxed extra in a month × 12 + untaxed extra in a month × 12 + one-off taxed + one-off untaxed + retirement income in a month × 12.

sections.name: taxableAnnual
sections.what_it_is_for: Taxable annual income (excludes non-taxable benefits/support/scholarships) — the base for tax estimates.
sections.formula_in_words: totalGrossAnnual WITHOUT the untaxed parts: salary + tips + bonus + signing bonus + stock vesting + net rent + taxed extra in a month × 12 + one-off taxed + retirement income in a month × 12. The 401(k) is NOT taken off here.

sections.name: monthlyTaxRates
sections.what_it_is_for: The tax rate for each of the twelve months, as a share: the one rate in force in every month — the person's own where they gave one, otherwise the calculated rate.
sections.formula_in_words: Twelve rates, all the same: the rate in force (rateInForce) — the person's own, or the calculated one. A steady income is taxed the same in every month.

sections.name: taxableByCalendarMonth
sections.what_it_is_for: The calendar-year TAXABLE profile (Jan→Dec) — the same placement rules incomeMonthlyGrid uses, extracted so the rate vector and the grid can never drift apart.
sections.formula_in_words: For each calendar month: gross salary + tips (only in months with salary) + net rent ÷ 12 + that month's stock vesting + taxed extra in a month + retirement income; + the bonus in its month (December when none); + the signing bonus in January; + one-off taxed other income in its month; − the household's 401(k) that month. Never below 0.

sections.name: incomeMonthlyGrid
sections.what_it_is_for: A representative 12-month cash-flow grid (Jan→Dec) that honors lumpiness: salary & net rental are steady every month; the annual bonus lands in December; the signing bonus is one-time (January); equity is the level annual vesting spread across the month-of-year its vest dates fall on (so quarterly vesting shows up as quarterly spikes).
sections.formula_in_words: For each calendar month. Earned before 401(k) = that month's taxed income (taxableByCalendarMonth) + that month's 401(k). Untaxed = support + that month's scholarships + benefits in their months + one-off untaxed income in its month. Gross = earned before 401(k) + untaxed − reinvested interest and dividends. Tax = tax on the wages + tax on the rest. The wages, earner by earner (worked in one place, which the Cash flow months read too): an earner who typed a take-home is taxed at their own share — (their yearly gross − their 401(k) for the year − 12 × the typed take-home) ÷ their yearly gross, held between 0 and 1 — so they land exactly what they typed; any other earner's wage × the rate in force (monthlyTaxRates). The rest (earned before 401(k) − the wages) × the rate in force — except that when the rate is the person's own, the month's rent and interest and dividends are left out, because they are not on a payslip. After-tax = gross − tax. Take-home = gross − tax − 401(k).

sections.name: guaranteedRows
sections.what_it_is_for: The dated guaranteed-income rows for the next 12 months (the F2 grid seam).
sections.formula_in_words: Nothing when the person's chosen income sources are listed without retirement income. Otherwise, over the twelve months starting with the current one, for Social Security, pension, annuity and other retirement income with an amount above zero: monthly → the amount in every month; quarterly → the amount in four months, three apart, starting at its named month (the current month when none); yearly → the amount once, in its named month (the current month when none). The amount is the amount of EACH PAYMENT.

sections.name: solveSafeDraw
sections.what_it_is_for: Largest level monthly draw that keeps chance-of-success ≥ the floor.
sections.formula_in_words: 0 when the savings are zero or less. Otherwise the largest monthly draw from the savings, on top of the guaranteed income, at which the retirement simulation (1,000 futures, fixed seed 42) still lasts to the horizon in at least 80 of 100. It is tried first at twice (savings ÷ years ÷ 12), $100 at least; then narrowed by halving 12 times; then rounded DOWN to the nearest $5.

sections.name: buildPaycheckYear
sections.what_it_is_for: Build the month-by-month paycheck.
sections.formula_in_words: Guaranteed rows from guaranteedRows; savings = the figure given, otherwise the accounts set aside for retirement (retirementEarmarkedValue, handed the profile's rent entries, DEC-4913). Safe draw = solveSafeDraw, with average guaranteed income in a month = the rows' total ÷ 12. Draw flag: high when safe draw × 12 ÷ savings is above 4.5%; ok otherwise; none with no savings or no draw. For each of twelve months from the current one: guaranteed total = that month's rows; bills = that month's big bills, everyday expenses left out; safe to spend = guaranteed total + safe draw − bills. This year = the twelve added.

sections.name: pctBaseMonthly
sections.what_it_is_for: A-1: the %-of-income base = true take-home (after tax AND 401k) — the SAME base the expenses-plan screen uses (modules.tsx SpendingEditor → takeHomeMonthly).
sections.formula_in_words: The twelve months of take-home (incomeMonthlyGrid, take-home) added ÷ 12.

sections.name: recurringDebtPayments
sections.what_it_is_for: RECURRING DEBT PAYMENTS — the installment debts, one row each.
sections.formula_in_words: One row for each debt whose payment is the same every month (an instalment loan): its name and its payment in this month — its required monthly payment from the month of its first payment to the month it is paid off (a date not given sets no bound), nothing outside them. Rows of zero are dropped. Cards, lines of credit and debts due in full are not here.

sections.name: debtPaymentsCountedAsExpenses
sections.what_it_is_for: DEBT PAYMENTS THAT ARE COUNTED AS EXPENSES — revolving and due-in-full.
sections.formula_in_words: For each debt that is NOT an instalment loan, and whose purchases are not already imported from a linked card: the payments logged this month under the category Debt payment whose payee matches the debt's name (capitals and outer spaces ignored), added up. A row only when that is above zero, named after the debt with the word payment.

sections.name: actualSpending
sections.what_it_is_for: What was actually spent in a month, debt payments left out: every expense newest first, the five shown, how many more there are and the totals, for all of them or only those entered by hand or only those imported.
sections.formula_in_words: The month's logged expenses, leaving out the category Debt payment, newest first — all of them, or only those entered by hand, or only those imported. Shown = the first 5. Hidden = how many more. Total = all of them added. Hidden total = total − the 5 shown.

sections.name: isRadarItem
sections.what_it_is_for: Whether a debt belongs on the big-ticket radar: yes for a card or a credit line and for a debt due in one lump, no for a loan paid the same every month.
sections.formula_in_words: An instalment loan: not a radar item. A debt due in full: a lump-sum item. Any other debt (a card, a line of credit): a revolving item.

sections.name: radar
sections.what_it_is_for: The big-ticket radar for a month: each card, credit-line or lump-sum debt payment and each large dated bill, with its amount and whether it is already counted as an expense.
sections.formula_in_words: For each debt that is a radar item (isRadarItem): amount = what was logged as paid against it this month when that is above zero, otherwise what falls due on it this month — its required payment from the month of its first payment to the month it is paid off, and for a debt due in full its whole balance in the month it is due; dropped when the amount is zero or less. It counts as an expense unless its purchases are already imported from a linked card. Then every big bill of $500 or more, with its due date, each counted as an expense. Debts first, bills after.

sections.name: rateInForce
sections.what_it_is_for: THE ONE ANSWER every screen reads.
sections.formula_in_words: In this order. (1) The person chose to type a rate: that percent ÷ 100, held between 0 and 1. (2) Yearly salary is above zero and every earner typed a take-home: rate = (yearly salary − 401(k) for the year − yearly take-home, never below 0) ÷ yearly salary, held between 0 and 1. Both of these count as the person's own. (3) Otherwise calculated: federal income tax plus state tax on the yearly taxed income (taxableAnnual) LESS the household's 401(k) contributions for the year — they come off before tax — ÷ the yearly taxed income, by filing status, with the standard deduction. 0 when there is no taxed income. Its words for what the calculated rate covers: federal income tax only — or, when a state rate was entered, federal income tax plus that state rate, written as a percent to two decimals — assuming the standard deduction.

sections.name: spendByMonthByBucket
sections.what_it_is_for: THE MONTH'S PLANNED EXPENSES, BY THE BUDGET'S OWN THREE GROUPS — each calendar month, January first (2026-10-23).
sections.formula_in_words: The month's planned expenses in the budget's three groups (bills and fixed, once in a while, everyday), for each of the 12 calendar months, January first. With categories, each category with an amount above 0 counts; one entered as a percent counts at amount ÷ 100 × the monthly take-home it is a share of (pctBaseMonthly). A once-in-a-while category's yearly amount (its amount, or for a percent that share × 12) falls in the months it names, split equally among them, or spread equally over all 12 when it names none; any other category counts its monthly amount in every month, under bills and fixed when it is a fixed bill and under everyday otherwise. While no category is a monthly one (only once-in-a-while categories), every month also gets the typed bills and fixed total and the typed everyday total, each in its own group. Without categories, every month gets the budget's three monthly totals (spendBuckets). Then every month's everyday expenses gain whatever the monthly spending entered is above what the plan puts in every month: the monthly categories, the typed totals counted above, and a once-in-a-while category that names no month at its twelfth. A once-in-a-while category that names its months is never counted against the monthly spending entered, so it adds to its own months only.

sections.name: expenses
sections.what_it_is_for: What is being spent this month: the debts that repeat every month, the planned expenses by category, what was actually spent by where it came from, and the big-ticket radar?
sections.formula_in_words: Recurring debt rows (recurringDebtPayments) and their total. Planned rows by category, as handed in, and their total. Actual expenses for the month — all, entered by hand, and imported (actualSpending). The debt payments that count as expenses (debtPaymentsCountedAsExpenses). Actual total = the actual expenses total + those debt payments. And the radar (radar).

sections.name: theBudgetCounted
sections.what_it_is_for: Which of my planned expenses are counted, now that my debts are taken from Debts?
sections.formula_in_words: Owner rule, 2026-10-04: "Once user enters mortgage or any debt - the app deduct it directly to calculate surplus, emergency fund, and any other place instead of leaving it for user to add it to planned expenses." The home = the property read as HOME (propertyUses, handed the profile's rent entries — none recorded is read as none, not as unknown). Its mortgage = the mortgage matched to that property (mortgagesByProperty). When the home has a mortgage in Debts AND the budget's Rent / Mortgage line holds an amount: that line is counted as nothing, the one typed monthly total (when there is one) is lowered by the same amount, never below zero, and the sentence says the line is not counted and names the mortgage. Otherwise — a renter, a home with no mortgage, a mortgage on another property, or no amount on the line — the budget is counted exactly as typed. It also names the home's mortgage when there is one. What the person typed is never changed; this is the budget as it is counted.

sections.name: earmarkDefault
sections.what_it_is_for: Default % of an account that's earmarked for retirement (rest funds other goals).
sections.formula_in_words: The share of an account counted towards retirement by default (owner, 2026-08-11, DEC-0100: all assets minus the home lived in and the car driven): 0% for a 529, for the car driven (primaryCarIdOf), and for the home lived in. Told the household's home (its identifier, from primaryHomeIdOf), only that property is 0%; told the household has no home (null), no property is; told nothing, a property stated as the home lived in, or with no use stated, is 0%. 100% for everything else — a rental, a second home, a second car, valuables included.

sections.name: primaryCarIdOf
sections.what_it_is_for: The vehicle treated as "the car you drive" — the most valuable one, so a second car stays a real asset.
sections.formula_in_words: Among the accounts whose kind is vehicle, and no other: the vehicles whose value is entered are the candidates — a vehicle with no value is not ranked as $0 (DEC-4036j, 2026-10-10); when none has a value, every vehicle is. Of the candidates, the one with the largest balance; a tie goes to the lower id read as text (the one made first). Nothing when there is no vehicle. Valuables and other personal property are never the car.

sections.name: earmarkedAmount
sections.what_it_is_for: The retirement-earmarked $ for one account (uses the saved % or the smart default).
sections.formula_in_words: Balance × the share earmarked for retirement. The share is the one stated on the account, held between 0% and 100%, or the default (earmarkDefault, told which car is driven and which property is lived in, or that there is none) when none is stated.

sections.name: retirementEarmarkedValue
sections.what_it_is_for: Total nest egg = sum of each account's retirement-earmarked portion.
sections.formula_in_words: Every account's earmarked amount (earmarkedAmount) added up, with the car driven found by primaryCarIdOf and the home lived in by primaryHomeIdOf, handed the Income screen's rent entries when the caller has them (DEC-4913, 2026-10-13). Example: A $400,000 with no use stated, B $300,000 marked the home with rent entered for B → $700,000 (B a rental, A a second home, no home). Not handed the rent entries, the stored home mark decides: $400,000.

sections.name: mortgagesByProperty
sections.what_it_is_for: Which mortgage is on which property, and which mortgages are on none.
sections.formula_in_words: Properties = the accounts whose class is real estate. Mortgages = the debts whose type is mortgage. Owner rule, 2026-10-04: "It is feasible to have property without mortgage but no mortgage without property. So check should be 3 properties in NW - 3 or less mortgage." A mortgage is on the property it names, when that property exists and has no mortgage placed on it yet. A mortgage that names no property is placed only where there is one answer: first, on the one property without a mortgage whose name its own name begins with; then, when exactly one property is still without a mortgage and exactly one mortgage is still without a property, on that property. Every other mortgage is listed as on no property — including a second mortgage that names a property already taken. It gives: the count of properties and of mortgages; for each property its mortgage (or none) and that mortgage's required monthly payment; the mortgages on no property; whether there are none of those; and the sentence to show when there are.

sections.name: propertyUses
sections.what_it_is_for: What each property is used for: the home lived in, a rental, or a second or vacation home.
sections.formula_in_words: For each property: what it is used for, as propertyUseMap reads it, handed the rent entries from the Income screen (none handed in when the person has none on record). Owner rule, 2026-10-04: "unless rental income is added on the income screen, assume property is second or vacation home." RENTAL = a rent entry names it — or, only when no rent entries are handed in at all, it is stored as a rental. HOME = the one marked as the home lived in; with none marked and no use stated on any, the one entered first. SECOND = every other property. A rent entry that names no property is not rent: it makes no property a rental (DEC-4059d, 2026-10-10). A use stated on any property stops the entered-first choice of the home (DEC-4913, 2026-10-13).

sections.name: primaryHomeIdOf
sections.what_it_is_for: Which property is the home lived in: the one marked so; with none marked and no use stated on any, the one entered first; otherwise none.
sections.formula_in_words: The property propertyUseMap reads as the home lived in, handed the rent entries when the caller has them. Nothing (null) when the household has no home — which is not the same as not being asked. Example (owner, 2026-10-13): B marked the home with a rent entry naming B, A with no use stated → null (B is a rental, A a second home).

sections.name: propertyUseMap
sections.what_it_is_for: What each property is for — the home lived in, a rental, or a second home — by his rule DEC-1926: a rental only when a rent entry on the Income screen names it; the one marked as the home is the home; with none marked and no use stated on any, the one entered first; every other property is a second home.
sections.formula_in_words: For each real-estate account: rental when a live rent entry names it, or — only when no rent entries were handed in at all (unknown, not none) — when it is stored as a rental. Of the rest: the one marked as the home lived in is home. With none of the rest marked, the one entered first (last in the list) that is not stored as a rental is home — but ONLY when no property at all carries a stated use other than rental (owner, 2026-10-13: a 'primary' mark on a property a rent entry made a rental still counts as a stated use, so it stops this; a stored 'rental' word does not). A property stored as a rental is never made the home this way. Every other property is a second home. A rent entry that names no property makes no property a rental (owner rule DEC-4059d, 2026-10-10 — it used to make the one other property a rental when exactly one remained).

sections.name: paymentNotEntered
sections.what_it_is_for: A DEBT WHOSE MONTHLY PAYMENT WAS NEVER ENTERED (2026-10-21, DEC-3523 tenet 3: unknown is not zero): neither a minimum nor a payment is on record as a number.
sections.formula_in_words: Whether a debt's monthly payment was never entered: neither its minimum payment nor its payment is on record as a number. A typed 0 is entered; a debt due in one lump has no monthly payment and is never named. The emergency fund (MK-NW-O-004) and the Net worth door (MK-NW-O-003) name such a debt beside their debt payments instead of counting it as $0 (owner decision DEC-3523, tenet 3: unknown is not zero).

sections.name: requiredPayment
sections.what_it_is_for: The payment reserved/required each month for a debt (planned payment, else the minimum).
sections.formula_in_words: 0 for a debt due in full. Otherwise the larger of the minimum monthly payment and the payment the person says they make.

sections.name: totalDebtMonthly
sections.what_it_is_for: Total monthly debt obligation across all debts (override-aware).
sections.formula_in_words: requiredPayment added over the debts.

sections.name: minimumDebtService
sections.what_it_is_for: The minimum payments every debt requires in a month, added up, leaving out any debt due in one lump on a date.
sections.formula_in_words: Each debt's minimum monthly payment added; a debt due in full counts 0.

sections.name: actualDebtPayment
sections.what_it_is_for: Σ ACTUAL payments (override ≥ minimum) — what actually leaves your account.
sections.formula_in_words: The same as totalDebtMonthly: requiredPayment added over the debts.

sections.name: recurringDebtPayments
sections.what_it_is_for: RECURRING DEBT PAYMENTS — the installment debts, one row each.
sections.formula_in_words: One row for each debt whose payment is the same every month (an instalment loan): its name and its payment in this month — its required monthly payment from the month of its first payment to the month it is paid off (a date not given sets no bound), nothing outside them. Rows of zero are dropped. Cards, lines of credit and debts due in full are not here.

sections.name: debtPaymentsCountedAsExpenses
sections.what_it_is_for: DEBT PAYMENTS THAT ARE COUNTED AS EXPENSES — revolving and due-in-full.
sections.formula_in_words: For each debt that is NOT an instalment loan, and whose purchases are not already imported from a linked card: the payments logged this month under the category Debt payment whose payee matches the debt's name (capitals and outer spaces ignored), added up. A row only when that is above zero, named after the debt with the word payment.

sections.name: paymentInMonth
sections.what_it_is_for: WHAT A DEBT ASKS FOR IN ONE CALENDAR MONTH: nothing in a month no payment falls in (paysInMonth); in one that does, the whole balance for a debt due in full, and its payment (requiredPayment) for any other.
sections.formula_in_words: What a debt asks for in one calendar month: 0 in a month no payment of it falls in (paysInMonth); in a month one does, the whole balance for a debt due in full, and its required payment for any other.

sections.name: savingsByMonth
sections.what_it_is_for: Discretionary amount free to save each month = take-home that month (after tax & 401k) minus the expenses due that month.
sections.formula_in_words: For each calendar month: the take-home that month (incomeMonthlyGrid, take-home) − the planned expenses that month (spendByMonth).

sections.name: annualCashflow
sections.what_it_is_for: ONE annual cash-flow roll-up, derived entirely from the per-month income grid + spendByMonth — the SAME bases the savings-plan and budget already use.
sections.formula_in_words: Gross for the year, after-tax for the year and take-home for the year = the twelve months of incomeMonthlyGrid in each of its three modes, added. Expenses for the year = spendByMonth added. Tax = gross − after-tax. 401(k) = after-tax − take-home. Saved = take-home − expenses.

sections.name: publishSurplus
sections.what_it_is_for: Publish the authoritative surplus for Goals/Retirement to consume.
sections.formula_in_words: Announces the projected-to-save figure to the rest of the app, unchanged.

sections.label: Expenses
sections.answers: What you plan to spend in this month, as one line on the flow — and the total of the Expenses tab's planned rows.
sections.formula: this month's planned expenses = bills & fixed + once-in-a-while bills that fall in this month + everyday expenses (spendByMonthByBucket, the budget as counted) — a once-a-year bill counts in its own month, never a twelfth; a once-in-a-while bill with no month set is a twelfth a month
decisions: One line on This month, and the Expenses tab is its detail — not a second answer to the same question (his correction, 2026-09-28).

A bill that lands once a year is planned in the month it lands, never spread (his DEC-0002 and DEC-0447; MK-CF-M-048). A budget whose only line falls in another month reads $0 this month, not "not set" (2026-10-23).
sections.refusal: No budget set — on This month the row reads "— not set", and under the rows a sentence says there is no planned surplus until a budget is set ("… we won’t guess one.") with the door "Set your budget"; on Expenses the band reads — with "You haven’t set your budget yet. …" and the same door. Income not entered — the month is not drawn: its two set-up steps stand in its place.

worked.given: September 2026: $7,200 take-home; a $2,400 mortgage and a $250 car loan due; a $3,400 budget ($2,300 rent, $700 groceries, $400 eating out). Logged so far: $2,300 rent, $512 groceries, $186 eating out, and the $250 car loan paid. The Plan already promises $300/month to the emergency fund.

sections.label: = Planned surplus
sections.answers: The surplus in the month if everything goes to plan.
sections.formula: the inflow, less every debt payment due, less the budget, less each big-ticket item
decisions: EVERY ROW SHOWN IS A ROW DEDUCTED (his rule under the approved design): nothing appears on This month without being in the sum.
sections.refusal: No planned surplus is shown, and the band reads —: when no budget is set (the sentence under the rows says so and offers "Set your budget"), or when a debt’s payment was never entered ("Car loan’s payment is not entered, so there is no planned surplus — we won’t guess one.", 2026-10-23). Income not entered — the month is not drawn: its two set-up steps stand in its place.

worked.given: September 2026: $7,200 take-home; a $2,400 mortgage and a $250 car loan due; a $3,400 budget ($2,300 rent, $700 groceries, $400 eating out). Logged so far: $2,300 rent, $512 groceries, $186 eating out, and the $250 car loan paid. The Plan already promises $300/month to the emergency fund.

sections.label: = Actual surplus so far
sections.answers: What is actually left, on what has really happened so far this month.
sections.formula: the inflow received, less each debt actually paid, less everything logged by hand and imported
decisions: An unpaid debt shows $0 with its due date — never silently dropped, or the surplus would flatter the month.
A card payment is counted ONCE: connected card → the imported purchases are the expense and the payment is a radar note; not connected → the payment IS the expense.
sections.refusal: Nothing logged and no card linked — it says so and offers the door.

worked.given: September 2026: $7,200 take-home; a $2,400 mortgage and a $250 car loan due; a $3,400 budget ($2,300 rent, $700 groceries, $400 eating out). Logged so far: $2,300 rent, $512 groceries, $186 eating out, and the $250 car loan paid. The Plan already promises $300/month to the emergency fund.

sections.label: each row of the month — what it is and what it costs
sections.answers: One line per thing in or out this month, so the surplus can be checked by reading down the column — and, on Expenses, each line of its lists.
sections.formula: one row per line of the month, each at its own amount. This month, planned: the inflow, each debt's payment due, the month's planned expenses, each big-ticket item. This month, actual: the inflow, each debt's payment made so far ($0 with its due day when nothing was), other debt payments, the expenses entered by hand and imported. Expenses: each debt that repeats every month at its payment, the total of the repeating debts, and each list's total of what was logged
decisions: Drawn from the approved design (cash-flow_v01): the flow is SPELLED OUT, not summarised into three numbers.
sections.refusal: A row whose amount is not known says so where the amount would be: "— not set" for a budget not set, "payment not entered" for a debt whose payment was never entered (2026-10-23). A debt not paid yet shows $0 with its due day ("not paid yet" when no due day is recorded). Nothing logged: "Expenses entered by hand" stays at a real $0, with "Nothing logged yet, and no card connected. …" under the rows. On Expenses every section keeps its heading when empty, at a real $0.

worked.given: September 2026: $7,200 take-home; a $2,400 mortgage and a $250 car loan due; a $3,400 budget ($2,300 rent, $700 groceries, $400 eating out). Logged so far: $2,300 rent, $512 groceries, $186 eating out, and the $250 car loan paid. The Plan already promises $300/month to the emergency fund.

sections.label: Actual expenses
sections.answers: What has actually gone out so far this month, from the expenses logged.
sections.formula: every expense logged inside the month, added up — a debt payment logged as an expense is counted with the debts, not here
sections.refusal: Nothing logged in the month — a real $0 on the ACTUAL EXPENSES band, with "Nothing logged this month. Connect a card and purchases arrive on their own, or add a receipt by hand." and the door "Log an expense".

worked.given: September 2026: $7,200 take-home; a $2,400 mortgage and a $250 car loan due; a $3,400 budget ($2,300 rent, $700 groceries, $400 eating out). Logged so far: $2,300 rent, $512 groceries, $186 eating out, and the $250 car loan paid. The Plan already promises $300/month to the emergency fund.

sections.label: each expense and its amount
sections.answers: One logged expense — where, when, how much.
sections.formula: the amount as logged
sections.refusal: Nothing logged in the month — the list is not drawn; "Nothing logged this month. …" and the door "Log an expense" stand in its place.

worked.given: September 2026: $7,200 take-home; a $2,400 mortgage and a $250 car loan due; a $3,400 budget ($2,300 rent, $700 groceries, $400 eating out). Logged so far: $2,300 rent, $512 groceries, $186 eating out, and the $250 car loan paid. The Plan already promises $300/month to the emergency fund.

sections.label: Planned expenses — each category
sections.answers: For each of the budget's groups — bills & fixed, once in a while, everyday expenses: what is planned for it in this month.
sections.formula: planned = the group's planned expenses for this month (spendByMonthByBucket, the budget as counted): bills & fixed and everyday expenses every month, a once-in-a-while bill only in the months it falls; a group with nothing planned this month is not drawn; the rows add up to MK-CF-M-001
sections.refusal: No budget set — the categories are not drawn: the band reads —, with "You haven’t set your budget yet. This is what every “of $X planned” on any screen is measured against." and the door "Set your budget".

worked.given: September 2026: $7,200 take-home; a $2,400 mortgage and a $250 car loan due; a $3,400 budget ($2,300 rent, $700 groceries, $400 eating out). Logged so far: $2,300 rent, $512 groceries, $186 eating out, and the $250 car loan paid. The Plan already promises $300/month to the emergency fund.

sections.label: THIS MONTH — free to use
sections.answers: The planned surplus, less what the Plan has already promised to goals this month — what is genuinely free.
sections.formula: = Planned surplus (MK-CF-M-002) − the goals’ commitments (MK-CF-M-021)
decisions: A PROMISE TO A GOAL IS MONEY ALREADY SPOKEN FOR — it never reads as free.
sections.refusal: No budget set, or a debt’s payment never entered (2026-10-23) — no line: nothing is called free until there is a plan to be free of.

worked.given: September 2026: $7,200 take-home; a $2,400 mortgage and a $250 car loan due; a $3,400 budget ($2,300 rent, $700 groceries, $400 eating out). Logged so far: $2,300 rent, $512 groceries, $186 eating out, and the $250 car loan paid. The Plan already promises $300/month to the emergency fund.

sections.label: <goal> · from your Plan
sections.answers: What the Plan sends to one goal each month, shown on This month as a line already spoken for.
sections.formula: the goal’s monthly amount, as the Plan set it
sections.refusal: No goal with a monthly amount — no line.

worked.given: September 2026: $7,200 take-home; a $2,400 mortgage and a $250 car loan due; a $3,400 budget ($2,300 rent, $700 groceries, $400 eating out). Logged so far: $2,300 rent, $512 groceries, $186 eating out, and the $250 car loan paid. The Plan already promises $300/month to the emergency fund.

sections.label: Planned inflow
sections.grain: one figure per household per month
sections.answers: What the plan says comes in during a month after this one — printed on that month’s plan card, and as the Income tab’s expected take-home for the month shown.
sections.formula: planned inflow = the dated grid’s inflow for that month: Σ of every income source that lands in that month, at its take-home amount (after tax and 401(k)); a source that lands once a year counts only in the month it lands
decisions: A month is a real calendar month, never a twelfth of a year (founder, 2026-08-28).
sections.refusal: Shows $0 until income is entered, with the door to enter it.
sections.note: Printed by the plan card of a later month (“Planned inflow”) and by the Income tab (“expected take-home”, this month or the month picked), both from the dated grid’s cell for that month.

worked.given: On 15 Sep 2026, October’s plan card: $7,200/month take-home; a $3,400/month budget; a $2,400 mortgage and a $250 car loan.

sections.label: Planned outflow (expenses + debt)
sections.grain: one figure per household per month
sections.answers: What the plan says goes out during a month after this one — printed on that month’s plan card: the budget, the debt payments that fall in that month, and any big bill that falls in it.
sections.formula: planned outflow = the dated grid’s outflow for that month: the month’s planned expenses (a bill with its own month in that month only) + each debt payment that falls in that month (from its first payment to its payoff; a balance due in full once, in its month)
decisions: A debt payment is counted as an outflow, not as saving (founder, 2026-06-21).
A bill that falls once a year is shown in its own month, never spread.
A debt counts in a month only if a payment falls in that month — the rule This month’s planned surplus (MK-CF-M-002) reads too (2026-10-24).
sections.refusal: Shows $0 until expenses or debts are entered.
sections.note: Printed by the plan card of a later month only, from the dated grid’s cell for that month.

worked.given: On 15 Sep 2026, October’s plan card: $7,200/month take-home; a $3,400/month budget; a $2,400 mortgage and a $250 car loan.

sections.label: = Planned surplus
sections.grain: one figure per household per month
sections.answers: What the plan leaves over in a month after this one — printed on that month’s plan card.
sections.formula: planned surplus = planned inflow − planned outflow, as the card prints them (the dated grid’s cell for that month)
sections.refusal: Shows $0 until both sides are entered.
sections.note: Printed by the plan card of a later month only. This month’s planned surplus is MK-CF-M-002; the retired view’s “Spent $X of $Y surplus” line prints MK-CF-M-078 (until 2026-10-24 it was printed under this number).

worked.given: On 15 Sep 2026, October’s plan card: $7,200/month take-home; a $3,400/month budget; a $2,400 mortgage and a $250 car loan.

sections.label: each planned line
sections.grain: one figure per line per month
sections.answers: Each thing the plan says comes in or goes out this month, named, so the two totals can be checked by hand.
sections.formula: one line per source or commitment that falls in this month, at its amount for this month
sections.refusal: The list is replaced by the door to enter income or expenses when nothing is entered.

worked.given: September 2026: $7,200 take-home; a $2,400 mortgage and a $250 car loan due; a $3,400 budget. Logged so far: $2,300 rent, $512 groceries, $186 eating out, and the $250 car loan paid.

sections.label: Inflow
sections.grain: one figure per household per month
sections.answers: What has come in this month on the actual side: the month’s take-home, as the approved drawing draws it — before any paycheck is recorded as received.
sections.formula: inflow = the month’s take-home — this month’s cell of the dated grid: every source that lands in this month, after tax and 401(k); a payment recorded as received is listed under RECEIVED on the Income tab (MK-CF-M-012) and is not added to it
decisions: THE APPROVED DRAWING WINS (2026-10-23, under his rules DEC-3523 tenet 6 and "the newest approval wins", 2026-09-27): cash-flow_v01, approved 2026-09-28 (DEC-0440), draws the month’s take-home as Actual inflow with nothing recorded. The words this row carried — "nothing is assumed to have arrived; a source counts only once it is recorded" (2026-08-28) — are older and stand down. To reverse: count only recorded payments here, and Cash flow and Home move together.
Home prints this same figure, from the same rows (2026-10-23): it added any income recorded as received on top of the take-home, which Cash flow does not.
sections.refusal: Income not entered: $0, and under it the one line "Nothing entered yet. Add your income ›" on Home (Q48); Cash flow draws no month until income is entered — its two set-up steps stand in its place.
sections.note: The words beside it name what is inside it — "Inflow (income (take-home) + rent)" — his cluster 5 ruling of 2026-09-10.

worked.given: September 2026: $7,200 take-home; a $2,400 mortgage and a $250 car loan due; a $3,400 budget. Logged so far: $2,300 rent, $512 groceries, $186 eating out, and the $250 car loan paid.

sections.label: Outflow (expenses + debt)
sections.grain: one figure per household per month
sections.answers: What has actually gone out so far this month: the expenses logged and the debt payments made.
sections.formula: Outflow (expenses + debt) so far = MK-CF-F-194 monthOutflow of the expenses logged so far this month and the debt payments made so far; an unpaid debt shows $0 with its due day
decisions: A debt payment counts once it is made — logged as a debt payment — and an unpaid debt shows $0 with its due day, never left off (the approved drawing, DEC-0440).
Home prints this same figure, from the same rows (2026-10-23): it used to count the expenses only, without the debt paid.
sections.refusal: A real $0 when nothing is logged and no debt is paid. Cash flow draws no month until income is entered (its two set-up steps); a past month with no record reads "Nothing recorded for this month — it predates your tracking."

worked.given: September 2026: $7,200 take-home; a $2,400 mortgage and a $250 car loan due; a $3,400 budget. Logged so far: $2,300 rent, $512 groceries, $186 eating out, and the $250 car loan paid.

sections.label: = Surplus
sections.grain: one figure per household per month
sections.answers: What is actually left this month so far — not what the plan said, what has happened.
sections.formula: surplus so far = inflow so far − outflow so far
decisions: ONE FIGURE ON TWO SCREENS (2026-10-23, DEC-0345 and tenet 4): Home's "Left" is the Cash flow tab's "= Actual surplus so far", read from the same rows — Home showed $4,202 against Cash flow's $3,952 for one month because it left out the $250 car loan paid.
sections.refusal: Income not entered: no surplus — Cash flow shows its two set-up steps, and Home's box reads — beside Left, with "Nothing entered yet. Add your income ›" under Income and no pace word. A past month with no record: $0 and "Nothing recorded for this month — it predates your tracking."
sections.note: The Cash flow screen used to subtract this itself (rule 5). It is the door’s figure now.

worked.given: September 2026: $7,200 take-home; a $2,400 mortgage and a $250 car loan due; a $3,400 budget. Logged so far: $2,300 rent, $512 groceries, $186 eating out, and the $250 car loan paid.

sections.label: each received line
sections.answers: Each line of the actual side of the month, named — the inflow, each debt paid or still due, the expenses — so the actual surplus can be checked by hand.
sections.formula: one line per row of the actual block, at its amount so far: the inflow; each debt, minus what was paid against it this month ($0 with its due day when nothing was); other debt payments; the expenses entered by hand and imported
sections.refusal: A real $0 on a line with nothing in it — a debt not paid yet reads $0 with its due day, and "Expenses entered by hand" stays at $0; Cash flow draws no month until income is entered.

worked.given: September 2026: $7,200 take-home; a $2,400 mortgage and a $250 car loan due; a $3,400 budget. Logged so far: $2,300 rent, $512 groceries, $186 eating out, and the $250 car loan paid.

sections.label: left of your budget
sections.answers: What is left of this month’s budget after what has been spent so far.
sections.formula: the budget (MK-CF-M-001) − spent so far (MK-CF-M-013); below zero it reads as over
sections.refusal: No budget set — nothing to be left of.

sections.his_words: cashflow. Approve.
sections.the_log_records:
Cash flow becomes ONE screen with four tabs, replacing the two separate Cash flow and Budget screens. Four decisions:
1. The Budget screen is RETIRED; its job moves onto the cash-flow surface.
2. Income is entered through a pop-up that asks whether your pay is steady or varies.
3. You can move between past and future months.
4. Big one-off bills get their own list, so a bill that lands once a year is not lost inside a monthly average.

headings: # Cash flow — part 14 of 19: This month — the plan and what has happened
## Notes for this part
## The app's own types these cards name
## The cards
## Formulas these cards lean on

## The figures these cards feed — as the screen register holds them
## The decisions that govern this part — one `rules_held` line for each

sections.name: basePay
sections.what_it_is_for: What does this household's base pay come to: each earner's pay, and the household's gross, tax bracket, tax, 401(k)s and take-home for a month?
sections.formula_in_words: Runs earnerPay for each earner with the household's filing status (single when none), the number of people 65 or over, and the household's rate in force (rateInForce). Yearly gross = the earners' yearly gross added up. Take-home = their monthly take-homes added up. Tax band = the federal band on ALL the earners' wages together less each earner's own 401(k) for the year (a 401(k) is not taxed), by filing status; the band on the first earner's wage less their own 401(k) is also worked out, and when there are two or more earners, the two bands differ, and every earner typed a take-home, a note says so. When there are two or more earners and every one typed a take-home, a sentence also says the rate in force is their own figures. When nobody typed a take-home the card states its own sum in words: gross in a month − tax − 401(k)s = take-home. Tax in a month = yearly gross × the rate in force ÷ 12. Mode: entered when every earner typed a take-home; calculated when none did; mixed otherwise. When the rate in force is the calculated one, short-by = Social Security and Medicare on each earner's yearly gross (payrollTaxWithheld), added up, ÷ 12; nothing otherwise. Every figure agrees only when every earner's check passes (payFiguresAgree). Monthly 401(k) = added up over the earners. Other taken in a month = each earner's everything-else added up; nothing when any earner's take-home is calculated. The sentence under the take-home, when every earner typed one: what they entered, nothing calculated — or, when the gross was worked back from a take-home entered the old way, that the take-home is what they entered and the gross was worked back from it.

sections.his_words: s against two people
sections.the_log_records:
The whole income surface redesigned. Six decisions:
1. Base pay becomes a full screen with one expandable section per earner — gross, 401(k), employer match, and what actually lands.
2. A 14-month dated table when pay varies, rather than one typical figure.
3. BOTH earners are captured, not one: a household on $84,000 plus $54,000 was being read as $84,000 — one person’s income against two people’s spending.
4. A filing-status question, which had never been asked, so every couple was taxed as a single filer.
5. Bonus and company shares follow the same who-earns pattern.
6. Interest and dividends are worked out from your holdings rather than asked for, and treated as TAXABLE BUT NOT SPENDABLE.

sections.his_words: "yes" — DEC-0178, confirmed as written: The tax band is produced ONCE, at total income (MK-CF-F-084 taxable annual → MK-CF-F-090 effective rate). The base-pay s
sections.the_log_records: Your tax band is worked out ONCE, from your total income, and every screen reads that one figure. The base-pay screen does not work out a band of its own — a band is set by everything you are taxed on together, so a screen that sees only your wage would show the wrong one.

The app carried TWO complete tax engines, both live from the same profile on the same day, and one of them could not read a filing status at all. One is deleted. ZERO numbers moved for a single filer — the two were identical arithmetic there — and it becomes correct for couples the moment the filing-status question lands.

sections.the_log_records:
Our tax estimate covers federal income tax only, and says so on the screen. Three decisions:
1. We do not add payroll tax to it. Payroll tax applies to wages, and our gross figure also holds rent, dividends and bonuses — applying 7.65% to all of that would be wrong, not just rough.
2. We do not guess state tax, because it cannot be known without asking.
3. We work out the one thing we can, name the gap in dollars, and let you correct it.

headings: # Cash flow — part 15 of 19: Base pay — gross, take-home, and the rate of tax in force
## Notes for this part
## The app's own types these cards name
## The cards
## Formulas these cards lean on
## The same idea, computed elsewhere — for comparison only
## The figures these cards feed — as the screen register holds them
## The decisions that govern this part — one `rules_held` line for each

sections.name: grossFromNet
sections.what_it_is_for: Invert the schedule: the gross income whose take-home equals `net` (bisection).
sections.formula_in_words: 0 when the take-home is zero or less. Otherwise it searches between the take-home and three times it, halving the range 50 times, for the gross at which gross − federal tax (taxOwedFor, no state tax) equals the take-home.
sections.handed: export function grossFromNet(net: number, status: FilingStatus = 'single', over65 = 0): number
inputs_it_reads: MK-XS-I-030 tax filing status and age
sections.period: No figure on screen names this function; its period is whatever its formula states.
sections.when_it_gives_no_number: Not recorded apart from the formula: read the formula for what it gives when an input is missing.

sections.name: progressiveMonthlyTax
sections.what_it_is_for: The tax taken in each of the twelve months when the brackets fill as the year's income builds up, so a month with a bonus is taxed higher and the twelve add up to the year's tax exactly.
sections.formula_in_words: For each month in order: the federal tax on the year's running total up to and including that month − the federal tax on the running total before it; plus state tax = the rise in taxable income over the same step × the state rate (held between 0 and 15%). A negative month counts 0.

sections.name: seniorDeductionFor
sections.what_it_is_for: How much of the $6,000-per-person senior deduction does this return get?
sections.formula_in_words: 0 outside tax years 2025 to 2028; when filing separately; when nobody is 65 or over; or when the income is not known. Otherwise each person 65 or over (2 at most) gets $6,000 less 6% of the income above $75,000 (single, head of household) or $150,000 (married), never below 0 — the 6% comes off each person's $6,000, not off the two together; the answer is that amount × the number of those people.

sections.name: convertTakeHomeMode
sections.what_it_is_for: Convert it. What they typed becomes what LANDS; the gross is worked back once and stored.
sections.formula_in_words: Unchanged unless it needs converting (needsTakeHomeConversion). Otherwise: yearly take-home = the stored figure × the periods in a year (weekly 52, every two weeks 26, monthly 12, hourly counted as 12); yearly gross = when the person typed their own rate (a rate of 0% up to, not including, 100%): (the yearly take-home + 12 × their monthly 401(k)) ÷ (1 − that rate), so their rate and their take-home both hold; otherwise the gross whose federal tax leaves exactly that take-home (grossFromNet); the stored base pay becomes yearly gross ÷ periods; the typed take-home becomes the yearly take-home ÷ 12 — the month every screen now asks for; the mode becomes gross; and the profile is marked as having its gross worked back, which Your base pay says until a gross is typed.

sections.name: effectiveTaxRate
sections.what_it_is_for: The share of gross income that goes to tax: the person's own rate where they gave one, otherwise the calculated federal rate for the way they file.
sections.formula_in_words: With the person's own rate switched on: that rate, held between 0 and 1. Otherwise federal income tax on the yearly gross ÷ the yearly gross, by filing status (single when none), with no state tax (effectiveRateOnGrossFor).

sections.name: effectiveRate
sections.what_it_is_for: The one tax rate in force for the household, as a share of gross: their own figure where they gave one, otherwise the calculated rate.
sections.formula_in_words: The rate in force (rateInForce).

sections.name: rateInForce
sections.what_it_is_for: THE ONE ANSWER every screen reads.
sections.formula_in_words: In this order. (1) The person chose to type a rate: that percent ÷ 100, held between 0 and 1. (2) Yearly salary is above zero and every earner typed a take-home: rate = (yearly salary − 401(k) for the year − yearly take-home, never below 0) ÷ yearly salary, held between 0 and 1. Both of these count as the person's own. (3) Otherwise calculated: federal income tax plus state tax on the yearly taxed income (taxableAnnual) LESS the household's 401(k) contributions for the year — they come off before tax — ÷ the yearly taxed income, by filing status, with the standard deduction. 0 when there is no taxed income. Its words for what the calculated rate covers: federal income tax only — or, when a state rate was entered, federal income tax plus that state rate, written as a percent to two decimals — assuming the standard deduction.

sections.name: taxableAnnual
sections.what_it_is_for: Taxable annual income (excludes non-taxable benefits/support/scholarships) — the base for tax estimates.
sections.formula_in_words: totalGrossAnnual WITHOUT the untaxed parts: salary + tips + bonus + signing bonus + stock vesting + net rent + taxed extra in a month × 12 + one-off taxed + retirement income in a month × 12. The 401(k) is NOT taken off here.

sections.name: taxedAfterPreTax
sections.what_it_is_for: WHAT THE YEAR IS TAXED ON ONCE THE 401(k)s ARE OUT — everything taxable (taxableAnnual) less each earner's own 401(k) for the months they are paid, never below $0.
sections.formula_in_words: What the year is taxed on once the 401(k)s are out: everything taxable over the year less the household's 401(k) contributions — each earner's own, for the months they are paid — added up; never below 0.

sections.name: taxableByCalendarMonth
sections.what_it_is_for: The calendar-year TAXABLE profile (Jan→Dec) — the same placement rules incomeMonthlyGrid uses, extracted so the rate vector and the grid can never drift apart.
sections.formula_in_words: For each calendar month: gross salary + tips (only in months with salary) + net rent ÷ 12 + that month's stock vesting + taxed extra in a month + retirement income; + the bonus in its month (December when none); + the signing bonus in January; + one-off taxed other income in its month; − the household's 401(k) that month. Never below 0.

sections.name: totalGrossAnnual
sections.what_it_is_for: Total annual income across every inflow (salary for months worked + bonus + signing + equity + net rental + self-employment/investment/benefits/support/scholarship/other).
sections.formula_in_words: Salary for the year + tips for the year + bonus + signing bonus + stock vesting + net rent + taxed extra in a month × 12 + untaxed extra in a month × 12 + one-off taxed + one-off untaxed + retirement income in a month × 12.

sections.name: deductionFor
sections.what_it_is_for: The amount of income that is free of tax before the brackets start: the standard deduction for the way the person files, plus the extra amounts for anyone 65 or older.
sections.formula_in_words: The standard deduction for the filing status + the age-65 addition × the number of people 65 or over (2 at most) + the senior deduction (seniorDeductionFor). The amounts are in the 2026 table above the cards.

sections.name: taxableIncomeFor
sections.what_it_is_for: What income is taxed, given how this person files?
sections.formula_in_words: Gross − the deduction (deductionFor, with the gross itself used as the income for the senior deduction's phase-out); never below 0.

sections.name: taxOwedFor
sections.what_it_is_for: Federal tax owed under a filing status, plus an optional user-set FLAT state rate applied to TAXABLE income (E10) — states differ wildly, so one honest user-entered percent beats fifty guessed tables, and it never taxes the deduction.
sections.formula_in_words: Taxable income (taxableIncomeFor) taxed band by band on the filing status's 2026 table — each slice at its own rate — plus taxable income × the state rate (held between 0 and 15%).

sections.name: effectiveRateOnGrossFor
sections.what_it_is_for: What share of my income actually goes in tax?
sections.formula_in_words: taxOwedFor ÷ gross; 0 when the gross is zero or less.

sections.name: rateInForce
sections.what_it_is_for: THE ONE ANSWER every screen reads.
sections.formula_in_words: In this order. (1) The person chose to type a rate: that percent ÷ 100, held between 0 and 1. (2) Yearly salary is above zero and every earner typed a take-home: rate = (yearly salary − 401(k) for the year − yearly take-home, never below 0) ÷ yearly salary, held between 0 and 1. Both of these count as the person's own. (3) Otherwise calculated: federal income tax plus state tax on the yearly taxed income (taxableAnnual) LESS the household's 401(k) contributions for the year — they come off before tax — ÷ the yearly taxed income, by filing status, with the standard deduction. 0 when there is no taxed income. Its words for what the calculated rate covers: federal income tax only — or, when a state rate was entered, federal income tax plus that state rate, written as a percent to two decimals — assuming the standard deduction.

sections.name: paidOutByAccount
sections.what_it_is_for: What each account actually PAID OUT in the last year, by account.
sections.formula_in_words: Dividends, interest and coupons dated within the last year (on or after the same date last year), not reinvested, and naming an account, added by account — each counted as the money it moved into the account: when the record says which way the money went, its size, minus when it left (a reversed payment takes away what it had added); otherwise its amount with the sign it was stored with; a record whose amount is not on record (missing, blank or not a number) adds nothing. A record that names no account is not counted.

sections.name: incomeFromAccounts
sections.what_it_is_for: One line per account that pays something, and the total.
sections.formula_in_words: For each account, the first that applies. (1) It paid out more than zero over the trailing twelve months (paidOutByAccount): that amount, said as paid out over the trailing twelve months. (2) A bond or CD, by the one rule for its year of interest (yearlyInterestNow): no rate entered → $0, said so (owner A46), marked as assumed; a rate but no year's interest — a bond with a maturity date and no face value — → $0, said to be the face value not entered, marked as assumed; past its maturity date → $0, said to be matured on that date; a face value entered → the rate × the face value; otherwise (a CD bought from the bank typed by its balance, or a bond fund) → the rate × the balance. (3) Cash with a rate above zero: rate × balance. (4) Any other account with a balance above zero is named as not counted; foreign currency is skipped. Yearly income = the rows added.

sections.name: seniorDeductionFor
sections.what_it_is_for: How much of the $6,000-per-person senior deduction does this return get?
sections.formula_in_words: 0 outside tax years 2025 to 2028; when filing separately; when nobody is 65 or over; or when the income is not known. Otherwise each person 65 or over (2 at most) gets $6,000 less 6% of the income above $75,000 (single, head of household) or $150,000 (married), never below 0 — the 6% comes off each person's $6,000, not off the two together; the answer is that amount × the number of those people.

sections.name: yearlyInterest
sections.what_it_is_for: A year's interest from one bond or CD, by the one rule every interest figure uses: face × rate; with no face entered, a bond or a CD bought through a broker that has a maturity date has none — its coupon is paid on the face, which is not entered — while a CD bought from the bank or a bond fund (no maturity date) pays its rate on its value; with no rate, nothing (owner A46: counted as $0, said so).
sections.formula_in_words: A year's interest from one bond or CD. Nothing when no rate was entered. Face value × rate when a face value was entered. With no face value entered: nothing for a bond, or a CD bought through a broker (pricedLikeBond), that has a maturity date — its coupon is paid on the face, so the rate on the market value would be a guess (the lead's decision of 2026-10-24 under owner decision DEC-3523, tenet 3); otherwise — a CD bought from the bank, typed by its balance, or a bond fund, which has no maturity date — the value shown × rate: the market value, else what was paid, else the face value, and 0 when no value was entered (owner decision DEC-0281 for the value shown; owner ruling DEC-2748c, 2026-10-07, for face × rate and, with no face, value × rate).

sections.name: yearlyInterestNow
sections.what_it_is_for: A year's interest from one bond or CD as it pays today: its yearly interest, and $0 once it is past its maturity date.
sections.formula_in_words: A year's interest from one bond or CD as it pays today: $0 once it is past its maturity date; otherwise its yearly interest (yearlyInterest: face × rate; with no face, nothing for a bond with a maturity date, and the value × rate for a CD bought from the bank or a bond fund), and nothing when no rate was entered.

sections.name: pricedLikeBond
sections.what_it_is_for: (DEC-3837, 2026-10-10) THE ONE TEST of whether a holding is priced like a bond: every bond is, and a CD only when it was bought through a broker.
sections.formula_in_words: Yes for every bond that is not a CD. For a CD: yes only when it was bought through a broker; a CD bought from the bank, or one whose answer was never given, is no (DEC-3837, 2026-10-10). This is the one test every bond figure reads to decide whether a CD is priced like a bond.

sections.name: effectiveRateOnGrossFor
sections.what_it_is_for: What share of my income actually goes in tax?
sections.formula_in_words: taxOwedFor ÷ gross; 0 when the gross is zero or less.

sections.name: rateInForce
sections.what_it_is_for: THE ONE ANSWER every screen reads.
sections.formula_in_words: In this order. (1) The person chose to type a rate: that percent ÷ 100, held between 0 and 1. (2) Yearly salary is above zero and every earner typed a take-home: rate = (yearly salary − 401(k) for the year − yearly take-home, never below 0) ÷ yearly salary, held between 0 and 1. Both of these count as the person's own. (3) Otherwise calculated: federal income tax plus state tax on the yearly taxed income (taxableAnnual) LESS the household's 401(k) contributions for the year — they come off before tax — ÷ the yearly taxed income, by filing status, with the standard deduction. 0 when there is no taxed income. Its words for what the calculated rate covers: federal income tax only — or, when a state rate was entered, federal income tax plus that state rate, written as a percent to two decimals — assuming the standard deduction.

sections.name: taxableIncomeFor
sections.what_it_is_for: What income is taxed, given how this person files?
sections.formula_in_words: Gross − the deduction (deductionFor, with the gross itself used as the income for the senior deduction's phase-out); never below 0.

sections.name: ageAttainedInYear
sections.what_it_is_for: THE AGE THE LIMITS USE — the age a person attains at any time in the calendar year, which is this year minus the birth year.
sections.formula_in_words: This calendar year − the birth year. Nothing when the birth year is missing or before 1900.

sections.his_words: Which 12 months are you entering?
sections.the_log_records:
When you enter a year of income, the app asks which twelve months you mean — the calendar year, or the next twelve months from now. Three decisions:
1. Every month you enter carries its own month AND year, so entering across a New Year does not overwrite the wrong month.
2. Both ways of asking write to the same twelve calendar slots underneath, so the answer means the same thing however it was entered.
3. When a receipt is scanned, the total is read from the total — never from a line about how it was paid, which is not what you spent.

sections.his_words: yes, I like the text.
sections.the_log_records: “yes, I like the text.” The Social Security card is approved in two versions: at 60 and 61 it says the decision is coming up, that you can first claim at 62, and that every year you wait after that raises the amount — so the card is honest about what you cannot do yet.

sections.his_words: s against two people
sections.the_log_records:
The whole income surface redesigned. Six decisions:
1. Base pay becomes a full screen with one expandable section per earner — gross, 401(k), employer match, and what actually lands.
2. A 14-month dated table when pay varies, rather than one typical figure.
3. BOTH earners are captured, not one: a household on $84,000 plus $54,000 was being read as $84,000 — one person’s income against two people’s spending.
4. A filing-status question, which had never been asked, so every couple was taxed as a single filer.
5. Bonus and company shares follow the same who-earns pattern.
6. Interest and dividends are worked out from your holdings rather than asked for, and treated as TAXABLE BUT NOT SPENDABLE.

sections.his_words: by default = reinvested). The onboarding dividends screen now asks
sections.the_log_records: Dividends and interest come OUT of your spendable take-home, because in most accounts they are reinvested where they are earned and never reach your bank. The onboarding screen asks “Does this reach your bank?” and says what the answer means.

sections.his_words: takehome
sections.the_log_records: When you type your take-home instead of your gross, it is converted ONCE on the way in and stored. The old code re-ran the tax schedule backwards on EVERY read to find a gross that would produce your figure — a guess laid on top of an estimate.

sections.his_words: explained and fixed in the file: the four mis-rendered functions written by hand; caps declared
sections.the_log_records: “explained and fixed in the file: the four mis-rendered functions written by hand; caps declared.” Four calculations the automatic reader could not render faithfully were written out by hand rather than left as a bad approximation.

sections.his_words: a figure the person gave us → 'you entered'
sections.the_log_records: “a figure the person gave us → ‘you entered’.” One phrase for a number you typed, so it is never confused with one the app worked out.

sections.his_words: spouse
sections.the_log_records: “spouse.” The word is spouse, not partner, in everything a person reads.

sections.his_words: an unknown input produces no number and a reason — never a default
sections.the_log_records: “an unknown input produces no number and a reason — never a default.” Where something is not known, the app says what is missing instead of filling in a plausible figure. A default looks like an answer.

sections.his_words: flat pensions are being inflated — a fixed-versus-inflating flag per stream; Social Security inflates, pensions and annuities flat
sections.the_log_records: “flat pensions are being inflated — a fixed-versus-inflating flag per stream; Social Security inflates, pensions and annuities flat.” Each income stream says whether it rises with inflation. Inflating a fixed pension overstates a retirement by more every year.

sections.his_words: withdrawals and RMDs are not guaranteed income — paycheck lists each line; the plan input is outside money only
sections.the_log_records: “withdrawals and RMDs are not guaranteed income — paycheck lists each line; the plan input is outside money only.” Money you draw from your own savings is not guaranteed income; only money arriving from outside is. Counting your own pot as guaranteed makes a plan look safe because it is spending itself.

sections.his_words: state tax applies to taxable income, never gross
sections.the_log_records: “state tax applies to taxable income, never gross.” Applying a state rate to gross income overstates the tax by the whole deduction.

sections.his_words: Q5 — the mortgage odds placeholder → build the second simulation first; until then the row states today’s odds and stops
sections.the_log_records: “Q5 — the mortgage odds placeholder → build the second simulation first; until then the row states today’s odds and stops.” Rather than showing a placeholder figure, the row says what is true today and says nothing more until the calculation exists.

sections.his_words: how about one time income?
sections.the_log_records: “how about one time income?” Income that arrives once is captured as such and lands in its own month, rather than being spread across twelve.

sections.his_words: How is the amount calculated by age? Is this a formula used by social security administration?
sections.the_log_records: HIS QUESTION: “How is the amount calculated by age? Is this a formula used by the Social Security Administration?” Asking whether a figure follows the actual rules or our approximation of them.

sections.his_words: How all this information will be captured and at what frequency?
sections.the_log_records: HIS QUESTION: “How all this information will be captured and at what frequency?” Including the parts no connection can reach — cash, and cards that are not linked.

His ruling DEC-0283 (2026-09-10): income before tax is gross less the 401(k) and other deductions. The tax was already worked that way while the bracket named the band of the gross. 5 of 5 places now read the income after the 401(k). The Income summary bracket, single, $70,000 of wages and $10,000 into a 401(k): 22% on $53,900 → 12% on $43,900, tax about $5,020 unchanged. Sign-up's Taxes step shows the same 12%. Your base pay, the drawing's own household, $138,000 of wages and $14,400 into 401(k)s, taxed on $91,400: 22% → 12%. The filing-status comparison works its tax after the 401(k), its line naming what was entered less the 401(k). The draw-order sheet's rates are worked after the 401(k). Base pay's 12% is A FIGURE ON HIS APPROVED DRAWING (income-end-to-end v07, phone 2, which draws 22%), applied under tenet 1, which ranks above tenet 6, with the correction line his DEC-4529 asks for on the drawing. sections.the_log_records: NOT A DECISION OF HIS — the lead's decision of 2026-10-24 under his ruling DEC-0321, made without asking him, as his order of 2026-09-30 says. His ruling DEC-0321 (2026-08-20): one tab said state tax was missing from the capital-gains figure and one said included; settled in one place. Its number stays on the register's retired list with this reason. To reverse: restore the function and drop the two sentences. One word from him reverses it.

headings: # Cash flow — part 17 of 19: Tax on the household — what is taxed, the filing status, the rates, and the tax organizer
## Notes for this part
## The cards

sections.label: Expenses
sections.answers: What you plan to spend in this month, as one line on the flow — and the total of the Expenses tab's planned rows.
sections.formula: this month's planned expenses = bills & fixed + once-in-a-while bills that fall in this month + everyday expenses (spendByMonthByBucket, the budget as counted) — a once-a-year bill counts in its own month, never a twelfth; a once-in-a-while bill with no month set is a twelfth a month
decisions: One line on This month, and the Expenses tab is its detail — not a second answer to the same question (his correction, 2026-09-28).

A bill that lands once a year is planned in the month it lands, never spread (his DEC-0002 and DEC-0447; MK-CF-M-048). A budget whose only line falls in another month reads $0 this month, not "not set" (2026-10-23).
sections.refusal: No budget set — on This month the row reads "— not set", and under the rows a sentence says there is no planned surplus until a budget is set ("… we won’t guess one.") with the door "Set your budget"; on Expenses the band reads — with "You haven’t set your budget yet. …" and the same door. Income not entered — the month is not drawn: its two set-up steps stand in its place.

worked.given: September 2026: $7,200 take-home; a $2,400 mortgage and a $250 car loan due; a $3,400 budget ($2,300 rent, $700 groceries, $400 eating out). Logged so far: $2,300 rent, $512 groceries, $186 eating out, and the $250 car loan paid. The Plan already promises $300/month to the emergency fund.

sections.label: = Planned surplus
sections.answers: The surplus in the month if everything goes to plan.
sections.formula: the inflow, less every debt payment due, less the budget, less each big-ticket item
decisions: EVERY ROW SHOWN IS A ROW DEDUCTED (his rule under the approved design): nothing appears on This month without being in the sum.
sections.refusal: No planned surplus is shown, and the band reads —: when no budget is set (the sentence under the rows says so and offers "Set your budget"), or when a debt’s payment was never entered ("Car loan’s payment is not entered, so there is no planned surplus — we won’t guess one.", 2026-10-23). Income not entered — the month is not drawn: its two set-up steps stand in its place.

worked.given: September 2026: $7,200 take-home; a $2,400 mortgage and a $250 car loan due; a $3,400 budget ($2,300 rent, $700 groceries, $400 eating out). Logged so far: $2,300 rent, $512 groceries, $186 eating out, and the $250 car loan paid. The Plan already promises $300/month to the emergency fund.

sections.label: = Actual surplus so far
sections.answers: What is actually left, on what has really happened so far this month.
sections.formula: the inflow received, less each debt actually paid, less everything logged by hand and imported
decisions: An unpaid debt shows $0 with its due date — never silently dropped, or the surplus would flatter the month.
A card payment is counted ONCE: connected card → the imported purchases are the expense and the payment is a radar note; not connected → the payment IS the expense.
sections.refusal: Nothing logged and no card linked — it says so and offers the door.

worked.given: September 2026: $7,200 take-home; a $2,400 mortgage and a $250 car loan due; a $3,400 budget ($2,300 rent, $700 groceries, $400 eating out). Logged so far: $2,300 rent, $512 groceries, $186 eating out, and the $250 car loan paid. The Plan already promises $300/month to the emergency fund.

sections.label: each row of the month — what it is and what it costs
sections.answers: One line per thing in or out this month, so the surplus can be checked by reading down the column — and, on Expenses, each line of its lists.
sections.formula: one row per line of the month, each at its own amount. This month, planned: the inflow, each debt's payment due, the month's planned expenses, each big-ticket item. This month, actual: the inflow, each debt's payment made so far ($0 with its due day when nothing was), other debt payments, the expenses entered by hand and imported. Expenses: each debt that repeats every month at its payment, the total of the repeating debts, and each list's total of what was logged
decisions: Drawn from the approved design (cash-flow_v01): the flow is SPELLED OUT, not summarised into three numbers.
sections.refusal: A row whose amount is not known says so where the amount would be: "— not set" for a budget not set, "payment not entered" for a debt whose payment was never entered (2026-10-23). A debt not paid yet shows $0 with its due day ("not paid yet" when no due day is recorded). Nothing logged: "Expenses entered by hand" stays at a real $0, with "Nothing logged yet, and no card connected. …" under the rows. On Expenses every section keeps its heading when empty, at a real $0.

sections.label: YOUR SOURCES — Base salary
sections.answers: Each earner’s base pay, as it was entered, with whether it was entered before tax or as take-home.
sections.formula: the base salary of each earner, in the period it was entered
inputs: MK-XS-I-060 how a person is paid — weekly, fortnightly, monthly
decisions: NEVER CONVERTED SILENTLY: the amount is shown in the period it was entered, and the period is said beside it.
sections.refusal: No salary entered — the row does not appear; the door to enter it does.

sections.label: YOUR SOURCES — Self-employment
sections.answers: Self-employment income, net, in the period it was entered.
sections.formula: the self-employment amount as entered, monthly or yearly
sections.refusal: None entered — the row does not appear.

worked.given: The two earners above, plus $24,000/year of self-employment, a $12,000 bonus in March, 50 shares vesting at $400, a rental bringing in $2,000/month against $800 of costs, and $2,100/month of Social Security.

sections.label: YOUR SOURCES — Bonus

sections.formula: the bonus as entered, a year; shown in the month it lands, never spread
inputs: MK-XS-I-059 the month a bonus lands
decisions: A LUMP THAT LANDS ONCE IS NEVER AVERAGED across the year (founder, 2026-08-28).
sections.refusal: None entered — the row does not appear.

worked.given: The two earners above, plus $24,000/year of self-employment, a $12,000 bonus in March, 50 shares vesting at $400, a rental bringing in $2,000/month against $800 of costs, and $2,100/month of Social Security.

sections.label: YOUR SOURCES — Stock vesting (equity)
sections.answers: What vests in a year, valued at the price entered.
sections.formula: shares vesting × price per share; with a grant schedule, the total ÷ the years it vests over
sections.refusal: No equity entered — the row does not appear.

worked.given: The two earners above, plus $24,000/year of self-employment, a $12,000 bonus in March, 50 shares vesting at $400, a rental bringing in $2,000/month against $800 of costs, and $2,100/month of Social Security.

sections.label: YOUR SOURCES — Rental property
sections.answers: What the rental brings in each month after its running costs.
sections.formula: (rent − running costs) for each rental, added up
sections.refusal: No rental entered — the row does not appear.
