sections.label: YOUR SOURCES — Social Security · pension
sections.answers: Guaranteed income being received now — Social Security, pension, annuity and other — in a month.
sections.formula: Social Security + pension + annuity + other, each brought to a monthly amount
sections.refusal: None being received — the row does not appear.

worked.given: The two earners above, plus $24,000/year of self-employment, a $12,000 bonus in March, 50 shares vesting at $400, a rental bringing in $2,000/month against $800 of costs, and $2,100/month of Social Security.

sections.label: RECEIVED · <month> — each payment
sections.answers: Each payment that has actually arrived this month, and when.
sections.formula: the income records dated inside the month
sections.refusal: Nothing received yet this month.

worked.given: Two $3,600 salary payments landed in September, on the 15th and the 30th; one landed on 31 August.

sections.label: Actual expenses
sections.answers: What has actually gone out so far this month, from the expenses logged.
sections.formula: every expense logged inside the month, added up — a debt payment logged as an expense is counted with the debts, not here
sections.refusal: Nothing logged in the month — a real $0 on the ACTUAL EXPENSES band, with "Nothing logged this month. Connect a card and purchases arrive on their own, or add a receipt by hand." and the door "Log an expense".

worked.given: September 2026: $7,200 take-home; a $2,400 mortgage and a $250 car loan due; a $3,400 budget ($2,300 rent, $700 groceries, $400 eating out). Logged so far: $2,300 rent, $512 groceries, $186 eating out, and the $250 car loan paid. The Plan already promises $300/month to the emergency fund.

sections.label: each expense and its amount
sections.answers: One logged expense — where, when, how much.
sections.formula: the amount as logged
sections.refusal: Nothing logged in the month — the list is not drawn; "Nothing logged this month. …" and the door "Log an expense" stand in its place.

worked.given: September 2026: $7,200 take-home; a $2,400 mortgage and a $250 car loan due; a $3,400 budget ($2,300 rent, $700 groceries, $400 eating out). Logged so far: $2,300 rent, $512 groceries, $186 eating out, and the $250 car loan paid. The Plan already promises $300/month to the emergency fund.

sections.label: Planned expenses — each category
sections.answers: For each of the budget's groups — bills & fixed, once in a while, everyday expenses: what is planned for it in this month.
sections.formula: planned = the group's planned expenses for this month (spendByMonthByBucket, the budget as counted): bills & fixed and everyday expenses every month, a once-in-a-while bill only in the months it falls; a group with nothing planned this month is not drawn; the rows add up to MK-CF-M-001
sections.refusal: No budget set — the categories are not drawn: the band reads —, with "You haven’t set your budget yet. This is what every “of $X planned” on any screen is measured against." and the door "Set your budget".

worked.given: September 2026: $7,200 take-home; a $2,400 mortgage and a $250 car loan due; a $3,400 budget ($2,300 rent, $700 groceries, $400 eating out). Logged so far: $2,300 rent, $512 groceries, $186 eating out, and the $250 car loan paid. The Plan already promises $300/month to the emergency fund.

sections.label: BIG-TICKET RADAR — <bill> · due <month>
sections.answers: A bill big enough to plan for, and the month it falls in.
sections.formula: the dated bills above the everyday size, in date order
decisions: A regular monthly debt is never a radar item: a warning you see every month stops being a warning.
sections.refusal: Nothing unusual ahead — the section keeps its heading and says so.

worked.given: On 28 Sep 2026, with $8,000 in the account: car insurance of $1,400 due 15 Oct and property tax of $4,800 due 1 Nov. Nothing else is dated.

sections.label: THIS MONTH — free to use
sections.answers: The planned surplus, less what the Plan has already promised to goals this month — what is genuinely free.
sections.formula: = Planned surplus (MK-CF-M-002) − the goals’ commitments (MK-CF-M-021)
decisions: A PROMISE TO A GOAL IS MONEY ALREADY SPOKEN FOR — it never reads as free.
sections.refusal: No budget set, or a debt’s payment never entered (2026-10-23) — no line: nothing is called free until there is a plan to be free of.

worked.given: September 2026: $7,200 take-home; a $2,400 mortgage and a $250 car loan due; a $3,400 budget ($2,300 rent, $700 groceries, $400 eating out). Logged so far: $2,300 rent, $512 groceries, $186 eating out, and the $250 car loan paid. The Plan already promises $300/month to the emergency fund.

sections.label: <goal> · from your Plan
sections.answers: What the Plan sends to one goal each month, shown on This month as a line already spoken for.
sections.formula: the goal’s monthly amount, as the Plan set it
sections.refusal: No goal with a monthly amount — no line.

sections.label: YOUR FUTURE PAYCHECK — At <age>: ~$X/month
sections.answers: About what a month would bring at retirement: the guaranteed income plus a level draw from the projected pot.
sections.formula: guaranteed income a month + the draw the projected pot can support (the paycheck year’s level draw)
decisions: AN ESTIMATE, SAID TO BE ONE on the screen — never a promise.
NOTHING BEFORE THERE IS A POT: with no accounts, or past retirement age, the card is not drawn.
sections.refusal: No pot to project from, or retirement age already reached — the card is not drawn.

worked.given: Born in 1981, retiring at 67, with $200,000 in a 401(k) earning 6% and $2,000/month of Social Security from 67.

sections.label: YOUR FUTURE PAYCHECK — Social Security · pension
sections.answers: The guaranteed part of that future month: Social Security, pension, annuity, other.
sections.formula: the outside guaranteed streams a month, added up
sections.refusal: No pot to project from, or retirement age already reached — the card is not drawn.

worked.given: Born in 1981, retiring at 67, with $200,000 in a 401(k) earning 6% and $2,000/month of Social Security from 67.

sections.label: each income source and its amount
sections.answers: Every source of income that has been entered, one line each, in the period it is counted in — a month or a year, said beside it.
sections.formula: each source as it was entered: rent after its running costs, in a month; interest and dividends, a bonus, scholarships and loans, in a year; the rest in a month
sections.refusal: Nothing entered — the list is replaced by the one line "Nothing entered yet. Add your income ›" (Q48), which opens Base pay.

worked.given: The two earners above, plus $24,000/year of self-employment, a $12,000 bonus in March, 50 shares vesting at $400, a rental bringing in $2,000/month against $800 of costs, and $2,100/month of Social Security. The line shown is the rental’s: what it brings in a month after its costs.

sections.label: Take-home
sections.answers: What actually reaches the bank each month, after federal tax and 401(k) — for one earner, and for the household.
sections.formula: for one earner: what they entered, or their gross less federal tax less their own 401(k). For the household: the sum of the earners’ figures, never a second calculation.
decisions: Federal income tax when it is calculated, plus the state rate when one was entered (the Tax organizer’s "State income tax %", applied to taxable income) — no Social Security or Medicare, and no state tax when none was entered (MK-CF-D-001, DEC-0384).
sections.refusal: Shows $0 until a wage is entered.
sections.note: ONE figure over two sets: one earner, and the household — so a total and its parts cannot disagree (rule 2). It wears ≈ whenever the figure was calculated rather than entered.

worked.given: Two earners filing jointly: $4,200 every two weeks ($109,200/year) and $5,000/month ($60,000), paying $1,200 and $400/month into their 401(k)s — $14,100/month of wages in all. They have typed their tax rate: 22%.

sections.label: Planned inflow
sections.grain: one figure per household per month
sections.answers: What the plan says comes in during a month after this one — printed on that month’s plan card, and as the Income tab’s expected take-home for the month shown.
sections.formula: planned inflow = the dated grid’s inflow for that month: Σ of every income source that lands in that month, at its take-home amount (after tax and 401(k)); a source that lands once a year counts only in the month it lands
decisions: A month is a real calendar month, never a twelfth of a year (founder, 2026-08-28).
sections.refusal: Shows $0 until income is entered, with the door to enter it.
sections.note: Printed by the plan card of a later month (“Planned inflow”) and by the Income tab (“expected take-home”, this month or the month picked), both from the dated grid’s cell for that month.

worked.given: On 15 Sep 2026, October’s plan card: $7,200/month take-home; a $3,400/month budget; a $2,400 mortgage and a $250 car loan.

sections.label: Planned outflow (expenses + debt)
sections.grain: one figure per household per month
sections.answers: What the plan says goes out during a month after this one — printed on that month’s plan card: the budget, the debt payments that fall in that month, and any big bill that falls in it.
sections.formula: planned outflow = the dated grid’s outflow for that month: the month’s planned expenses (a bill with its own month in that month only) + each debt payment that falls in that month (from its first payment to its payoff; a balance due in full once, in its month)
decisions: A debt payment is counted as an outflow, not as saving (founder, 2026-06-21).
A bill that falls once a year is shown in its own month, never spread.
A debt counts in a month only if a payment falls in that month — the rule This month’s planned surplus (MK-CF-M-002) reads too (2026-10-24).
sections.refusal: Shows $0 until expenses or debts are entered.
sections.note: Printed by the plan card of a later month only, from the dated grid’s cell for that month.

worked.given: On 15 Sep 2026, October’s plan card: $7,200/month take-home; a $3,400/month budget; a $2,400 mortgage and a $250 car loan.

sections.label: = Planned surplus
sections.grain: one figure per household per month
sections.answers: What the plan leaves over in a month after this one — printed on that month’s plan card.
sections.formula: planned surplus = planned inflow − planned outflow, as the card prints them (the dated grid’s cell for that month)
sections.refusal: Shows $0 until both sides are entered.
sections.note: Printed by the plan card of a later month only. This month’s planned surplus is MK-CF-M-002; the retired view’s “Spent $X of $Y surplus” line prints MK-CF-M-078 (until 2026-10-24 it was printed under this number).

worked.given: On 15 Sep 2026, October’s plan card: $7,200/month take-home; a $3,400/month budget; a $2,400 mortgage and a $250 car loan.

sections.label: each planned line
sections.grain: one figure per line per month
sections.answers: Each thing the plan says comes in or goes out this month, named, so the two totals can be checked by hand.
sections.formula: one line per source or commitment that falls in this month, at its amount for this month
sections.refusal: The list is replaced by the door to enter income or expenses when nothing is entered.

worked.given: September 2026: $7,200 take-home; a $2,400 mortgage and a $250 car loan due; a $3,400 budget. Logged so far: $2,300 rent, $512 groceries, $186 eating out, and the $250 car loan paid.

sections.label: Inflow
sections.grain: one figure per household per month
sections.answers: What has come in this month on the actual side: the month’s take-home, as the approved drawing draws it — before any paycheck is recorded as received.
sections.formula: inflow = the month’s take-home — this month’s cell of the dated grid: every source that lands in this month, after tax and 401(k); a payment recorded as received is listed under RECEIVED on the Income tab (MK-CF-M-012) and is not added to it
decisions: THE APPROVED DRAWING WINS (2026-10-23, under his rules DEC-3523 tenet 6 and "the newest approval wins", 2026-09-27): cash-flow_v01, approved 2026-09-28 (DEC-0440), draws the month’s take-home as Actual inflow with nothing recorded. The words this row carried — "nothing is assumed to have arrived; a source counts only once it is recorded" (2026-08-28) — are older and stand down. To reverse: count only recorded payments here, and Cash flow and Home move together.
Home prints this same figure, from the same rows (2026-10-23): it added any income recorded as received on top of the take-home, which Cash flow does not.
sections.refusal: Income not entered: $0, and under it the one line "Nothing entered yet. Add your income ›" on Home (Q48); Cash flow draws no month until income is entered — its two set-up steps stand in its place.
sections.note: The words beside it name what is inside it — "Inflow (income (take-home) + rent)" — his cluster 5 ruling of 2026-09-10.

worked.given: September 2026: $7,200 take-home; a $2,400 mortgage and a $250 car loan due; a $3,400 budget. Logged so far: $2,300 rent, $512 groceries, $186 eating out, and the $250 car loan paid.

sections.label: Outflow (expenses + debt)
sections.grain: one figure per household per month
sections.answers: What has actually gone out so far this month: the expenses logged and the debt payments made.
sections.formula: Outflow (expenses + debt) so far = MK-CF-F-194 monthOutflow of the expenses logged so far this month and the debt payments made so far; an unpaid debt shows $0 with its due day
decisions: A debt payment counts once it is made — logged as a debt payment — and an unpaid debt shows $0 with its due day, never left off (the approved drawing, DEC-0440).
Home prints this same figure, from the same rows (2026-10-23): it used to count the expenses only, without the debt paid.
sections.refusal: A real $0 when nothing is logged and no debt is paid. Cash flow draws no month until income is entered (its two set-up steps); a past month with no record reads "Nothing recorded for this month — it predates your tracking."

worked.given: September 2026: $7,200 take-home; a $2,400 mortgage and a $250 car loan due; a $3,400 budget. Logged so far: $2,300 rent, $512 groceries, $186 eating out, and the $250 car loan paid.

sections.label: = Surplus
sections.grain: one figure per household per month
sections.answers: What is actually left this month so far — not what the plan said, what has happened.
sections.formula: surplus so far = inflow so far − outflow so far
decisions: ONE FIGURE ON TWO SCREENS (2026-10-23, DEC-0345 and tenet 4): Home's "Left" is the Cash flow tab's "= Actual surplus so far", read from the same rows — Home showed $4,202 against Cash flow's $3,952 for one month because it left out the $250 car loan paid.
sections.refusal: Income not entered: no surplus — Cash flow shows its two set-up steps, and Home's box reads — beside Left, with "Nothing entered yet. Add your income ›" under Income and no pace word. A past month with no record: $0 and "Nothing recorded for this month — it predates your tracking."
sections.note: The Cash flow screen used to subtract this itself (rule 5). It is the door’s figure now.

worked.given: September 2026: $7,200 take-home; a $2,400 mortgage and a $250 car loan due; a $3,400 budget. Logged so far: $2,300 rent, $512 groceries, $186 eating out, and the $250 car loan paid.

sections.label: each received line
sections.answers: Each line of the actual side of the month, named — the inflow, each debt paid or still due, the expenses — so the actual surplus can be checked by hand.
sections.formula: one line per row of the actual block, at its amount so far: the inflow; each debt, minus what was paid against it this month ($0 with its due day when nothing was); other debt payments; the expenses entered by hand and imported
sections.refusal: A real $0 on a line with nothing in it — a debt not paid yet reads $0 with its due day, and "Expenses entered by hand" stays at $0; Cash flow draws no month until income is entered.

worked.given: September 2026: $7,200 take-home; a $2,400 mortgage and a $250 car loan due; a $3,400 budget. Logged so far: $2,300 rent, $512 groceries, $186 eating out, and the $250 car loan paid.

sections.label: Draw from savings
sections.answers: The level amount a month the pot can support, so the paycheck does not fall when a bill lands.
sections.formula: the paycheck year’s level draw from the pot, at the assumed return and horizon
decisions: IN TODAY’S DOLLARS (decided 2026-10-03, the master’s old Q30): the draw keeps its buying power — the figure shown is what it buys today, and the dollars paid rise with inflation each year. It is what the simulation behind the odds already charges, so the draw shown and the odds beside it are the same plan. To reverse: hold the dollars flat instead, and the odds must be re-run that way.
sections.refusal: No pot — no draw; the paycheck is the guaranteed income alone.

worked.given: Born in 1981, retiring at 67, with $200,000 in a 401(k) earning 6% and $2,000/month of Social Security from 67.

sections.label: left of your budget
sections.answers: What is left of this month’s budget after what has been spent so far.
sections.formula: the budget (MK-CF-M-001) − spent so far (MK-CF-M-013); below zero it reads as over
sections.refusal: No budget set — nothing to be left of.

worked.given: September 2026: $7,200 take-home; a $2,400 mortgage and a $250 car loan due; a $3,400 budget ($2,300 rent, $700 groceries, $400 eating out). Logged so far: $2,300 rent, $512 groceries, $186 eating out, and the $250 car loan paid. The Plan already promises $300/month to the emergency fund.

sections.label: /month interest
sections.answers: What your debts cost in interest in a month, at today’s balances and rates.
sections.formula: Σ balance × yearly rate ÷ 12, over every debt still owed
sections.refusal: No debts — $0.

worked.given: A $9,000 card at 24% with a $200 minimum and a $14,000 car loan at 6.9% with a $250 minimum, nothing extra paid.

sections.label: debt-free
sections.answers: How many months until the last debt is cleared, paying the minimums plus anything extra, highest rate first.
sections.formula: the payoff plan: each month pay every minimum, put the extra on the costliest debt, roll a cleared debt’s payment onto the next
sections.refusal: The payments cannot cover the interest — the screen says never, not a number.

worked.given: A $9,000 card at 24% with a $200 minimum and a $14,000 car loan at 6.9% with a $250 minimum, nothing extra paid.

sections.label: total interest
sections.answers: All the interest paid over the plan until the last debt is gone.
sections.formula: the interest paid month by month over the payoff plan, added up
sections.refusal: The payments cannot cover the interest — the screen says never, not a number.

sections.the_log_records:
Cash flow becomes ONE screen with four tabs, replacing the two separate Cash flow and Budget screens. Four decisions:
1. The Budget screen is RETIRED; its job moves onto the cash-flow surface.
2. Income is entered through a pop-up that asks whether your pay is steady or varies.
3. You can move between past and future months.
4. Big one-off bills get their own list, so a bill that lands once a year is not lost inside a monthly average.

sections.his_words: Which 12 months are you entering?
sections.the_log_records:
When you enter a year of income, the app asks which twelve months you mean — the calendar year, or the next twelve months from now. Three decisions:
1. Every month you enter carries its own month AND year, so entering across a New Year does not overwrite the wrong month.
2. Both ways of asking write to the same twelve calendar slots underneath, so the answer means the same thing however it was entered.
3. When a receipt is scanned, the total is read from the total — never from a line about how it was paid, which is not what you spent.

sections.the_log_records:
The whole income surface redesigned. Six decisions:
1. Base pay becomes a full screen with one expandable section per earner — gross, 401(k), employer match, and what actually lands.
2. A 14-month dated table when pay varies, rather than one typical figure.

4. A filing-status question, which had never been asked, so every couple was taxed as a single filer.
5. Bonus and company shares follow the same who-earns pattern.
6. Interest and dividends are worked out from your holdings rather than asked for, and treated as TAXABLE BUT NOT SPENDABLE.

headings: # Cash flow — part 18 of 19: The screens — the Cash flow tab, its four tabs, and Home's box for this month
## The figures — as the screen register holds them
## The cross-card checks for this part
## The decisions that govern this part — one `rules_held` line for each

sections.label: each source of guaranteed income
sections.answers: One line per guaranteed source — Social Security, a pension, an annuity, other — and what it pays a month.
sections.formula: each stream as entered, brought to a monthly amount
sections.refusal: Nothing entered — the list is replaced by the door to enter it.

worked.given: The two earners above, plus $24,000/year of self-employment, a $12,000 bonus in March, 50 shares vesting at $400, a rental bringing in $2,000/month against $800 of costs, and $2,100/month of Social Security.

sections.label: each bill and the day it falls
sections.answers: One line per bill ahead, with its date and what is left after it.
sections.formula: each dated bill in the window, in date order, with the running balance after it
decisions: A bill with NO date is not on the calendar — a date nobody gave would be read as one they did. It is still counted in the month’s total.
sections.refusal: No dated bill ahead — the COMING UP card is not drawn; with nothing behind the table at all, the one line "Nothing entered yet. Add your bills ›" sits under it (Q48).

worked.given: On 28 Sep 2026, with $8,000 in the account: car insurance of $1,400 due 15 Oct and property tax of $4,800 due 1 Nov. Nothing else is dated.

sections.label: Each person’s pay
sections.answers: What everyone in the household earns before anything is taken out.
sections.formula: gross a year = the sum of every earner’s wage, each annualised from the rhythm they are paid in
inputs: MK-CF-I-002 how often it is paid
decisions: A wage entered for a rhythm is annualised by that rhythm, never by a flat twelve.
sections.refusal: Shows $0 until a wage is entered; the screen offers the door to enter one.

worked.given: Two earners filing jointly: $4,200 every two weeks ($109,200/year) and $5,000/month ($60,000), paying $1,200 and $400/month into their 401(k)s — $14,100/month of wages in all. They have typed their tax rate: 22%.

sections.label: Federal tax bracket
sections.answers: What the next dollar earned costs in federal income tax.
sections.formula: the published bracket the household’s wages fall in once each earner’s own 401(k) is out — the 401(k) is not taxed — less the standard deduction, for their filing status
decisions: Filing status is assumed to be jointly when two people earn and nobody has said (MK-CF-D-004).
sections.refusal: The row is not shown until a wage is entered.

worked.given: Two earners filing jointly: $4,200 every two weeks ($109,200/year) and $5,000/month ($60,000), paying $1,200 and $400/month into their 401(k)s — $14,100/month of wages in all. They have typed their tax rate: 22%.

sections.label: Calculated federal tax
sections.answers: The federal income tax we calculate on the household’s wages, when nobody has entered their own figure.
sections.formula: tax a month = federal tax on (everything taxable, less the 401(k)s and the standard deduction, at the published bands) ÷ 12 — the same in every month
decisions: Assumes the standard deduction, never itemised (MK-CF-D-002).
sections.refusal: The row appears only when the figure is ours; an entered take-home already has tax inside it.

worked.given: One earner filing single: $5,000/month ($60,000/year), paying $400/month into a 401(k); no tax rate and no take-home told us, so the tax is ours. Taxed: $60,000 − $4,800 − $16,100 = $39,100 → $1,240 + 12% × $26,700 = $4,444/year, 7.41% of the $60,000.

sections.label: Your 401(k)s
sections.answers: What everyone in the household puts into their own 401(k) each month.
sections.formula: 401(k) a month = the sum of every earner’s own contribution, the employer’s match excluded
decisions: The employer’s match is not counted here — it is not taken out of take-home (MK-CF-D-003).
sections.refusal: The row is hidden when nobody contributes.

worked.given: Two earners filing jointly: $4,200 every two weeks ($109,200/year) and $5,000/month ($60,000), paying $1,200 and $400/month into their 401(k)s — $14,100/month of wages in all. They have typed their tax rate: 22%.

sections.label: The take-home above is higher than it will really be
sections.answers: By roughly how much the calculated take-home overstates what will reach the bank, because only federal income tax is taken out of it.
sections.formula: overstated by = Σ over earners of (Social Security 6.2% of the wage up to the wage base + Medicare 1.45% of the whole wage + 0.9% of the wage above the additional-tax threshold) ÷ 12
decisions: State tax is not in this figure, because we do not know their state (MK-CF-D-005).
sections.refusal: The warning appears only when the take-home is ours and estimated.

worked.given: Two earners filing jointly: $4,200 every two weeks ($109,200/year) and $5,000/month ($60,000), paying $1,200 and $400/month into their 401(k)s — $14,100/month of wages in all. They have told us no tax rate and no take-home, so the take-home shown is ours.

sections.label: Everything else taken out
sections.answers: What a payslip takes out beyond the 401(k) — tax, medical cover and anything else bought through work — read back from the figures the person entered.
sections.formula: for one earner: everything else = (their gross a year − their 401(k) a year − their take-home /year) ÷ 12. For the household: the sum of the earners’ figures, never a second subtraction.
decisions: Shown only when the person entered their own take-home, so the difference is theirs and not ours.
The household figure is the sum of the earners’, so a total and its parts cannot disagree (rule 2).
sections.refusal: The row is hidden for anyone whose take-home was calculated rather than entered; the household row is hidden unless every earner entered one.
sections.note: ONE figure over two sets: one earner, and the household. Moved off the screen into this door on 2026-09-14 — the base-pay card used to do the subtraction itself (rule 5).

worked.given: Two earners filing jointly: $4,200 every two weeks ($109,200/year) and $5,000/month ($60,000), paying $1,200 and $400/month into their 401(k)s — $14,100/month of wages in all. Each has typed their take-home each month: $5,850 and $3,400.

sections.label: Take-home each month
sections.answers: What reaches the bank in a usual month, from every source of income added together.
sections.formula: take-home a usual month = Σ of every source’s take-home in a usual month; a source that lands in one month of the year is not spread across twelve
decisions: A once-a-year source keeps its own month and is shown separately, never averaged in.
sections.refusal: Shows $0 on a fresh account, with the door to enter income — never a dash.
sections.note: FOUND BY THE WORKED EXAMPLE AND FIXED THE SAME DAY, 2026-09-28. This total read $9,798/month while the two take-home lines beneath it (MK-CF-M-038) added to $9,398 — $400 apart, exactly the spouse's monthly 401(k). MK-CF-F-060 salaryGrossByMonth sums EVERY earner's wage (his ruling, 2026-08-27) but the 401(k) taken off that household gross was written as the first earner's alone, so a spouse's was never subtracted — the take-home read too high by their contribution, and the taxable base too. NOT A NEW QUESTION: he ruled this on 2026-09-12 on income-end-to-end v07 — "one card disagreeing with itself; corrected to the take-home line" — and the correction reached the mock and not the code. Now MK-CF-F-206 householdK401ByMonth counts every earner in the months that earner is paid, and [a test of the app] holds the ruling. The six personas all passed throughout because none had a spouse with their own wage AND their own 401(k); twoEarnersBoth401k now does.

worked.given: Two earners filing jointly: $4,200 every two weeks ($109,200/year) and $5,000/month ($60,000), paying $1,200 and $400/month into their 401(k)s, with the tax rate typed at 22%.

sections.label: each source of take-home
sections.answers: What each source of income puts into the bank in a usual month, named and listed.
sections.formula: one line per source: the earner’s take-home, or the source’s monthly amount
sections.refusal: The list is replaced by the door to enter income when nothing is entered.

worked.given: Two earners filing jointly: $4,200 every two weeks ($109,200/year) and $5,000/month ($60,000), paying $1,200 and $400/month into their 401(k)s, with the tax rate typed at 22%.

sections.label: its own month, never spread
sections.answers: What the month a once-a-year source lands in brings in, all of it — the usual take-home plus that source after tax — shown in its own month rather than divided by twelve.
sections.formula: the standout month = of the twelve months’ take-home, the largest, when it is more than the usual month by over $1: its amount is that whole month’s take-home (the usual month plus the lump, after tax), its label the month’s name
decisions: A lump that lands once is never averaged across the year (founder, 2026-08-28).
sections.refusal: The line is hidden when no source behaves this way.

worked.given: The two earners above, plus $24,000/year of self-employment, a $12,000 bonus in March, 50 shares vesting at $400, a rental bringing in $2,000/month against $800 of costs, and $2,100/month of Social Security.

sections.label: is not here — it is reinvested where it is earned
sections.answers: Income that is taxed but never reaches the bank, so the two totals on this screen can be told apart.
sections.formula: taxed but not landed = interest and dividends earned inside accounts, which stay where they are earned
sections.refusal: The sentence is hidden when there is none.

worked.given: The two earners above, with $3,600/year of interest and dividends earned inside their accounts and left there.

sections.label: What it is taxed on
sections.answers: The whole year of income the tax is calculated on — the gross less the 401(k)s — a different number from the take-home, and said to be one.
sections.formula: what it is taxed on = gross a year (MK-CF-M-076) − the year's 401(k)s (MK-CF-M-077), never below $0 — his DEC-0283: income before tax is gross less the 401(k)
decisions: Income before tax is gross less the 401(k) and any other deduction; gross is before any deductions (DEC-0283, 2026-09-10).
sections.refusal: Shows $0 on a fresh account, with the door to enter income.

worked.given: Two earners filing jointly: $4,200 every two weeks ($109,200/year) and $5,000/month ($60,000), paying $1,200 and $400/month into their 401(k)s, with the tax rate typed at 22%.

sections.label: each taxed source
sections.answers: What each source contributes to the year the tax is calculated on.
sections.formula: one line per taxable source, at its yearly amount
sections.refusal: The list is replaced by the door to enter income when nothing is entered.

worked.given: Two earners filing jointly: $4,200 every two weeks ($109,200/year) and $5,000/month ($60,000), paying $1,200 and $400/month into their 401(k)s, with the tax rate typed at 22%.

sections.label: Federal tax bracket
sections.answers: What the next dollar costs in federal income tax, with every source counted, not wages alone.
sections.formula: the published bracket that what the year is taxed on falls in once the 401(k)s are out — every source counted, less each earner’s own 401(k), less the standard deduction — for their filing status
sections.refusal: The row is not shown until income is entered.
sections.note: The same concept as MK-CF-M-032 on the base-pay screen, over a wider base: that one counts wages, this one counts every source. Conflict C-5 on the orchestrator map asks whether they stay two figures.

worked.given: Two earners filing jointly: $4,200 every two weeks ($109,200/year) and $5,000/month ($60,000), paying $1,200 and $400/month into their 401(k)s, with the tax rate typed at 22%.

sections.label: Calculated federal tax
sections.answers: The federal income tax for the year, at whichever rate is in force — theirs if they entered one, ours if not.
sections.formula: tax a year = a rate typed by the person × the year's gross (MK-CF-M-076); when it is ours, federal tax on what it is taxed on (MK-CF-M-041: the gross less the 401(k)s) less the standard deduction, at the published bands — plus a state rate the person entered
inputs: MK-CF-M-041 what it is taxed on
decisions: When it is ours it assumes the standard deduction and is federal only, plus a state rate entered (MK-CF-D-002, DEC-7608).
The 401(k) comes off before tax (DEC-0283).
sections.refusal: The row is not shown until income is entered.

worked.given: The same two earners filing jointly, $169,200 of wages and $19,200 into their 401(k)s, with no tax rate typed. Taxed on $150,000; less the $32,200 standard deduction, $117,800 → $2,480 + $9,120 + 22% × $17,000 = $15,340.

sections.label: Social Security takes 6.2% of a wage up to
sections.answers: The wage ceiling above which no more Social Security tax is taken, named in the warning so the 6.2% can be checked.
sections.formula: the published wage base for the tax year
decisions: Published figure — the source and the year it applies to are on the master file’s Reference tab (guard D4).
sections.refusal: Never absent — it is a published figure, not a calculation.

worked.given: The payroll-tax figures Congress publishes for the 2026 tax year — not a calculation, and not ours to choose; they are read back so the sentence on screen can be checked against the law.

sections.label: Medicare 1.45% of everything, 0.9% more above
sections.answers: The wage above which the extra Medicare tax starts, named in the warning so the 0.9% can be checked.
sections.formula: the published additional-Medicare-tax threshold for the tax year
decisions: Published figure — the source and the year it applies to are on the master file’s Reference tab (guard D4).
sections.refusal: Never absent — it is a published figure, not a calculation.

worked.given: The payroll-tax figures Congress publishes for the 2026 tax year — not a calculation, and not ours to choose; they are read back so the sentence on screen can be checked against the law.

sections.label: Lowest point
sections.answers: The lowest the balance falls to in the twelve months ahead, and which month.
sections.formula: the smallest running balance across the twelve month-ends, starting from the balance you gave
sections.refusal: No starting balance — the table starts from $0 and says so.

worked.given: On 28 Sep 2026, with $8,000 in the account: car insurance of $1,400 due 15 Oct and property tax of $4,800 due 1 Nov. Nothing else is dated.

sections.label: END — where the month leaves you
sections.answers: The balance at the end of each month: the month before’s end, plus what came in, less what went out.
sections.formula: running balance = last month’s end + inflow − outflow, month by month from the starting balance
sections.refusal: No starting balance — the chain starts from $0 and says so.

worked.given: On 28 Sep 2026, with $8,000 in the account: car insurance of $1,400 due 15 Oct and property tax of $4,800 due 1 Nov. Nothing else is dated.

sections.label: Short — set it aside by <date>
sections.answers: How much more is needed for a bill by the day the money has to be there.
sections.formula: the bill − what is there by its need-by date (MK-CF-M-063, read from the month table), when that is less
sections.refusal: Nothing short — the line reads Covered instead.

worked.given: On 28 Sep 2026, with $8,000 in the account: car insurance of $1,400 due 15 Oct and property tax of $4,800 due 1 Nov. Nothing else is dated.

sections.label: Covered — about $X there by <date>
sections.answers: What is projected to be in the account on the day a bill’s money has to be there.
sections.formula: the month table’s End for the month before the need-by date (the starting balance when that day is in this month), plus what that month brings or takes on a day already passed — aid or a loan on the day it lands, a dated bill on its day (the 1st when it has none) — less the month’s regular money (pay, everyday expenses, debt payments) only when it takes out more than it brings in: the lower of the two month-ends either side of the day; less any bill listed above it that falls due after that day and by this bill’s due date
decisions: Read from the month table on the same screen, so this line and the End column cannot disagree.
Pay is never counted before its month ends: the table does not know the day it lands, and no day is invented.
sections.refusal: No balance to start from — nothing is projected.

worked.given: On 28 Sep 2026, with $8,000 in the account: car insurance of $1,400 due 15 Oct and property tax of $4,800 due 1 Nov. Nothing else is dated.

sections.label: Dividends, interest & coupons
sections.answers: What your holdings and bonds paid out over the last twelve months, from the records.
sections.formula: the dividend, interest and coupon records of the last twelve months, added up
sections.refusal: No record of any — $0, never an estimate.

worked.given: One account that recorded a $300 dividend in June and $120 of interest in March.

sections.label: Your guaranteed income
sections.answers: All the guaranteed income being received now, added up for a month.
sections.formula: the sum of each source of guaranteed income (MK-CF-M-024)
sections.refusal: Nothing entered — $0, with the door to enter it.

worked.given: The two earners above, plus $24,000/year of self-employment, a $12,000 bonus in March, 50 shares vesting at $400, a rental bringing in $2,000/month against $800 of costs, and $2,100/month of Social Security.

sections.label: = Gross /year
sections.answers: The whole year of income before any deductions — every taxable source, wages at gross.
sections.formula: gross a year = Σ of every taxable source over the year, wages included at gross, before any deductions
decisions: Gross is before any deductions (DEC-0283, 2026-09-10). It was printed as MK-CF-M-041 until 2026-10-24, when that became the income after the 401(k)s.
sections.refusal: Not shown on a fresh account — the door to enter income stands in the list.

worked.given: Two earners filing jointly: $4,200 every two weeks ($109,200/year) and $5,000/month ($60,000), paying $1,200 and $400/month into their 401(k)s, with the tax rate typed at 22%.

sections.label: Your 401(k)s
sections.answers: What every earner puts into their own 401(k) over the year — taken off the gross before tax.

The whole income surface redesigned. Six decisions:
1. Base pay becomes a full screen with one expandable section per earner — gross, 401(k), employer match, and what actually lands.
2. A 14-month dated table when pay varies, rather than one typical figure.

sections.the_log_records:
Our tax estimate covers federal income tax only, and says so on the screen. Three decisions:
1. We do not add payroll tax to it. Payroll tax applies to wages, and our gross figure also holds rent, dividends and bonuses — applying 7.65% to all of that would be wrong, not just rough.
2. We do not guess state tax, because it cannot be known without asking.
3. We work out the one thing we can, name the gap in dollars, and let you correct it.
